title.zh: 卷一百二十八 志第八十一 樂三
title.raw: 卷一百二十八 志第八十一 樂三 Volume 128 Treatises 81: Music 3

sentences.zh: 元豐三年五月，詔秘書監致仕劉幾赴詳定所議樂，以禮部侍郎致仕範鎮與幾參考得失。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered Liu Ji, who had retired from the Directorate of the Palace Library, to go to the deliberation office to discuss music, with Fan Zhen, who had retired as Vice Minister of Rites, to join Ji in weighing what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanfeng (1080), the throne ordered the retired palace librarian Liu Ji to attend the music deliberation office, with the retired Vice Minister of Rites Fan Zhen to assist him in judging what should stand and what should change.

sentences.zh: 而幾亦請命楊傑同議，且請如景祐故事，擇人修製大樂。

translations.literal: Ji also requested that Yang Jie be ordered to deliberate together, and further requested that, following the precedent of the Jingyou era, persons be chosen to revise and manufacture the great ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji also asked that Yang Jie be appointed to the same deliberation, and that people be selected to restore the great court music along the lines of the Jingyou precedent.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 初，言大樂七失：一曰歌不永言，聲不依永，律不和聲。

translations.literal: At the outset it was said that the great music had seven failures: first, that songs did not prolong the words, that tones did not follow the prolongation, and that pitch pipes did not harmonize with the sound.
translations.idiomatic: At first seven faults in the great music were identified. The first was that singing did not sustain the text, the melody did not follow that sustained utterance, and the pitch standards did not accord with the vocal line.

sentences.zh: 蓋金聲舂容，失之則重；

translations.literal: For metal sounds are measured and stately; if they err, they become heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Metal tones should be full and dignified; when they fail, they turn ponderous.

sentences.zh: 石聲溫潤，失之則輕；

translations.literal: Stone sounds are warm and moist; if they err, they become light.
translations.idiomatic: Stone tones should be rich and smooth; when they fail, they grow thin.

sentences.zh: 土聲函胡，失之則下；

translations.literal: Earth sounds are muffled; if they err, they become low.
translations.idiomatic: Earth tones should be rounded and deep; when they fail, they sink too low.

sentences.zh: 竹聲清越，失之則高；

translations.literal: Bamboo sounds are clear and piercing; if they err, they become high.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo tones should be bright and penetrating; when they fail, they rise too high.

sentences.zh: 絲聲纖微，失之則細；

translations.literal: Silk sounds are fine and subtle; if they err, they become thin.
translations.idiomatic: Silk tones should be delicate and refined; when they fail, they become faint.

sentences.zh: 革聲隆大，失之則洪；

translations.literal: Hide sounds are grand and great; if they err, they become booming.
translations.idiomatic: Hide tones should be powerful and expansive; when they fail, they swell to a roar.

sentences.zh: 匏聲叢聚，失之則長；

translations.literal: Gourd sounds are clustered together; if they err, they become prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd tones should gather in ensemble; when they fail, they drag on too long.

sentences.zh: 木聲無餘，失之則短。

translations.literal: Wood sounds have no surplus; if they err, they become short.
translations.idiomatic: Wood tones should be crisp without lingering; when they fail, they cut off too soon.

sentences.zh: 惟人稟中和之氣而有中和之聲，八音、律呂皆以人聲為度，言雖永，不可以逾其聲。

translations.literal: Only man receives the qi of central harmony and possesses the sound of central harmony; the eight tones and the pitch pipes all take the human voice as their measure, and though words may be prolonged, they cannot exceed that sound.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings alone embody the breath of perfect balance and produce balanced sound. The eight categories of instruments and the pitch pipes are all calibrated to the human voice; the text may be drawn out, but it must never outrun the voice that carries it.

sentences.zh: 今歌者或詠一言而濫及數律，或章句已闋而樂音未終，所謂歌不永言也。

translations.literal: Now singers sometimes chant one word and indiscriminately touch several pitch pipes, or the stanzas and lines are already ended while the musical tones have not yet ceased—this is what is called songs not prolonging the words.
translations.idiomatic: Today a singer may dwell on a single syllable while wandering across many notes, or the verse may already be finished while the melody still runs on. That is what is meant by singing that does not sustain the words.

sentences.zh: 請節其煩聲，以一聲歌一言。

translations.literal: It is requested that the excessive sounds be regulated, so that one sound sings one word.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that redundant notes be trimmed so that each syllable was carried by a single tone.

sentences.zh: 且詩言人誌，詠以為歌。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Odes express the will of man, and are chanted to become songs.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs gives voice to human intention and is sung as lyric.

sentences.zh: 五聲隨歌，是謂依詠；

translations.literal: The five tones follow the song—this is called following the chant.
translations.idiomatic: When the five tones follow the lyric, that is what is meant by 'following the chant.'

sentences.zh: 律呂協奏，是謂和聲。

translations.literal: The pitch pipes join in performance—this is called harmonizing the sound.
translations.idiomatic: When the pitch pipes join in concert, that is what is meant by 'harmonizing the sound.'

sentences.zh: 先儒以為依人音而製樂，托樂器以寫音，樂本效人，非人效樂者，此也。

translations.literal: The early Confucians held that music was made by relying on the human voice, entrusting instruments to write out the sound; music originally imitates man, not man imitating music—this is that principle.
translations.idiomatic: The early Confucians taught that music was fashioned from the human voice and that instruments merely notated it. Music takes its model from the person, not the person from the music—and that is the point.

sentences.zh: 今祭祀樂章並隨月律，聲不依詠，以詠依聲，律不和聲，以聲和律，非古製也。

translations.literal: Now the sacrificial music sections all follow the monthly pitch pipes; the sound does not follow the chant, but the chant follows the sound; the pitch pipes do not harmonize with the sound, but the sound harmonizes with the pitch pipes—this is not the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: At present the sacrificial hymns are all tied to the pitch of the month: melody does not follow the words, but the words are forced to follow the melody; the pipes do not harmonize with the voice, but the voice is bent to the pipes. That is not how the ancients arranged it.

sentences.zh: 二曰八音不諧，鍾磬闕四清聲。

translations.literal: Second: the eight tones are not in harmony, and the bells and chime-stones lack the four clear tones.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the eight categories of sound were not in harmony because the bells and stone chimes lacked the four 'clear' subsidiary pitches.

sentences.zh: 虞樂九成，以簫為主；

translations.literal: The music of Yu had nine performances, with the pan-pipe as master.
translations.idiomatic: In the music of Yu, the ninefold performance took the vertical flute as its leading voice.

sentences.zh: 商樂和平，以磬為依；

translations.literal: The music of Shang was peaceful and harmonious, with the sonorous stone as its basis.
translations.idiomatic: Shang music was serene and even, grounded on the stone chime.

sentences.zh: 周樂合奏，以金為首。

translations.literal: Zhou music was combined performance, with metal as the head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou music was ensemble playing led by metal percussion.

sentences.zh: 鍾、磬、簫者，眾樂之所宗，則天子之樂用八，鍾、磬、簫，眾樂之本，乃倍之為十六。

translations.literal: Bells, chime-stones, and pan-pipes are what all music takes as its model; thus the Son of Heaven's music uses eight, bells, chime-stones, and pan-pipes—the root of all music—and so they were doubled to make sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Bells, stone chimes, and flutes are the models for all music. The Son of Heaven's orchestra therefore used eight of them—bells, chimes, and flutes, the foundation of the ensemble—which were then doubled to sixteen.

sentences.zh: 且十二者，律之本聲；

translations.literal: Moreover, the twelve are the fundamental tones of the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve standard pitches are the root tones of the scale.

sentences.zh: 而四者，應聲也。

translations.literal: And the four are responsive tones.
translations.idiomatic: The four additional pitches are answering tones.

sentences.zh: 本聲重大為君父，應聲輕清為臣子，故其四聲曰清聲，或曰子聲也。

translations.literal: The fundamental tones are weighty and great as lord and father; the responsive tones are light and clear as minister and son; therefore the four tones are called clear tones, or also called son tones.
translations.idiomatic: Root tones are grave and commanding like a sovereign and father; answering tones are light and bright like a minister and son. Hence the four are called 'clear' tones, or 'son' tones.

sentences.zh: 李照議樂，始不用四清聲，是有本而無應，八音何從而諧哉？

translations.literal: When Li Zhao deliberated on music, he first did not use the four clear tones—there were fundamentals but no responses; how could the eight tones be harmonized?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhao revised the music, he first discarded the four clear pitches, leaving fundamentals without answers. Under those conditions the eight categories of sound could not possibly blend.

sentences.zh: 今巢笙、和笙，其管十九，以十二管發律呂之本聲，以七管為應聲。

translations.literal: Now the nest-sheng and the he-sheng have nineteen pipes; twelve pipes produce the fundamental tones of the pitch pipes, and seven pipes serve as responsive tones.
translations.idiomatic: The nest mouth-organ and the he mouth-organ each have nineteen pipes: twelve give the root pitches of the scale and seven supply the answering tones.

sentences.zh: 用之已久，而聲至和，則編鍾、磬、簫宜用四子聲以諧八音。

translations.literal: They have been used for a long time, and their sound is most harmonious; thus the arranged bells, chime-stones, and pan-pipes should use the four son tones to harmonize the eight tones.
translations.idiomatic: Long use has shown them to be perfectly consonant. The serial bells, stone chimes, and flutes should therefore adopt the four son tones to bring the eight categories into harmony.

sentences.zh: 三曰金石奪倫。

translations.literal: Third: metal and stone usurp the order.
translations.idiomatic: Third, metal and stone instruments overrode the proper order of the ensemble.

sentences.zh: 樂奏一聲，諸器皆以其聲應，既不可以不及，又不可以有餘。

translations.literal: When music plays one sound, all instruments respond with that sound; it cannot be less than it, nor can there be a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When the music strikes one note, every instrument should answer with that same note—neither falling short nor exceeding it.

sentences.zh: 今琴、瑟、塤、篪、笛、簫、笙、阮、箏、築奏一聲，則鎛鍾、特磬、編磬連擊三聲；

translations.literal: Now when the qin, se, ocarina, chi flute, vertical flute, pan-pipe, sheng, ruan, zheng, and zhu play one sound, the great bell, single chime-stone, and arranged chime-stones strike three sounds in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when the zither, harp, ocarina, chi, flute, pan-pipe, mouth-organ, ruan, zither-harp, and zhu sound a single note, the great bell, individual stone, and serial chimes strike three times in a row.

sentences.zh: 聲煩而掩眾器，遂至奪倫，則鎛鍾、特磬、編鍾、編磬節奏與眾器同，宜勿連擊。

translations.literal: The sound is vexatious and covers the other instruments, thus reaching the point of usurping order; then the great bell, single chime-stone, arranged bells, and arranged chime-stones should have the same rhythm as the other instruments and should not be struck in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The clamor drowns the other instruments and so usurps their place. The great bell, single stone, serial bells, and serial chimes should keep the same rhythm as the rest and should not be struck repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 四曰舞不象成。

translations.literal: Fourth: the dance does not image completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the dance did not embody the completed forms it was meant to represent.

sentences.zh: 國朝郊廟之樂，先奏文舞，次奏武舞，而武舞容節六變：一變象六師初舉，所向宜北；

translations.literal: In our dynasty's suburban and temple music, the civil dance is performed first, then the military dance; the military dance has six changes in its postures: the first change images the six armies first raising, and the direction faced should be north.
translations.idiomatic: At the state altars the civil dance is performed before the martial dance. The martial dance has six sections: the first depicts the six armies first taking the field, and the dancers should face north.

sentences.zh: 二變象上黨克平，所向宜北；

translations.literal: The second change images the pacification of Shangdang, and the direction faced should be north.
translations.idiomatic: The second depicts the conquest of Shangdang, again facing north.

sentences.zh: 三變象維揚底定，所向宜東南；

translations.literal: The third change images the settlement of Huainan, and the direction faced should be southeast.
translations.idiomatic: The third depicts the pacification of the Huai region, facing southeast.

sentences.zh: 四變象荊湖來歸，所向宜南；

translations.literal: The fourth change images the submission of Jinghu, and the direction faced should be south.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth depicts the submission of the Jing-Hu region, facing south.

sentences.zh: 五變象邛蜀納款，所向宜西；

translations.literal: The fifth change images the surrender of Qiong and Shu, and the direction faced should be west.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth depicts the surrender of Qiong and Shu, facing west.

sentences.zh: 六變象兵還振旅，所向宜北而南。

translations.literal: The sixth change images the army returning and marshaling the troops, and the direction faced should be from north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth depicts the army's return and muster, turning from north toward south.

sentences.zh: 今舞者發揚蹈厲、進退俯仰，既不足以稱成功盛德，失其所向，而文舞容節尤無法度，則舞不象成也。

translations.literal: Now the dancers' movements of brandishing and stamping, advancing and retreating, bowing and looking up, are insufficient to match the successful achievements and great virtue, and they lose the direction they should face; moreover the civil dance's postures especially have no standard—thus the dance does not image completion.
translations.idiomatic: Present performers stamp and brandish, advance and retreat, bow and rise, yet these movements no longer match the victories and virtues they are meant to celebrate, and they face the wrong directions. The civil dance in particular has lost all regulated form. That is why the dance no longer 'images completion.'

sentences.zh: 五曰樂失節奏。

translations.literal: Fifth: music loses rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the music had lost its rhythmic structure.

sentences.zh: 樂之始，則翕然如眾羽之合；

translations.literal: When music begins, it is suddenly like many feathers coming together.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of a piece, the sounds should gather the way many wings fold together.

sentences.zh: 縱之，純如也；

translations.literal: When released, it is pure and even.
translations.idiomatic: As it unfolds, it should flow pure and even.

sentences.zh: 節奏明白，如也；

translations.literal: The rhythm is clear and bright, even and right.
translations.idiomatic: The beat should stand out clear and steady.

sentences.zh: 往來條理，繹如也：然後成。

translations.literal: Coming and going in orderly sequence, continuous and unbroken: only then is it complete.
translations.idiomatic: Passages should move back and forth in orderly lines until the thread runs smooth and unbroken—only then is the performance complete.

sentences.zh: 今樂聲不一，混殽無敘，則失於節奏，非所謂成也。

translations.literal: Now the musical sounds are not unified, mixed and confused without order—thus it fails in rhythm, and is not what is called completion.
translations.idiomatic: Today the tones are not unified but jumbled without sequence, so the rhythm collapses and the performance never reaches true completion.

sentences.zh: 六曰祭祀、饗無分樂之序。

translations.literal: Sixth: sacrifice and feast lack the sequence of divided music.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, sacrifices and feasts lacked the proper alternation of instrumental and vocal music.

sentences.zh: 蓋金石眾作之謂奏，詠以人聲之謂歌。

translations.literal: For the combined performance of metal and stone is called zou (instrumental presentation), and chanting with the human voice is called ge (song).
translations.idiomatic: Ensemble playing on metal and stone is called zou; singing with the human voice is called ge.

sentences.zh: 陽律必奏，陰呂必歌，陰陽之合也。

translations.literal: Yang pitch pipes must be presented instrumentally, yin pitch pipes must be sung—this is the union of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang pitches must be played, yin pitches must be sung—that is the union of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 順陰陽之合，所以交神明、致精意。

translations.literal: Following the union of yin and yang is how to communicate with the spirits and concentrate the refined intent.
translations.idiomatic: By honoring that yin-yang pairing one communes with the spirits and gathers refined intention.

sentences.zh: 今冬至祀天，不歌大呂；

translations.literal: Now at the winter solstice sacrifice to Heaven, the Great Lu pitch is not sung.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice sacrifice to Heaven, the hymn in Great Lu is no longer sung.

sentences.zh: 夏至祭地，不奏太簇；

translations.literal: At the summer solstice sacrifice to Earth, the Great Cou pitch is not presented.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice sacrifice to Earth, the Great Cou pitch is no longer played.

sentences.zh: 春饗祖廟，不奏無射；

translations.literal: At the spring feast in the ancestral temple, the Wushe pitch is not presented.
translations.idiomatic: At the spring ancestral feast, the Wushe pitch is no longer played.

sentences.zh: 秋饗後廟，不歌小呂。

translations.literal: At the autumn feast in the rear temple, the Lesser Lu pitch is not sung.
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn feast in the rear shrine, the hymn in Lesser Lu is no longer sung.

sentences.zh: 而四望山川無專祠用樂之製，則何以讚導宣發陰陽之氣而生成萬物哉？

translations.literal: Yet for the four [directional] observances of mountains and rivers there is no dedicated ritual music system—then how can one praise, guide, proclaim, and release the qi of yin and yang to generate the myriad things?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the rites for the four directional mountains and rivers have no fixed music of their own. How then can music praise, guide, and release the breath of yin and yang so that the myriad things may be brought forth?

sentences.zh: 七曰鄭聲亂雅。

translations.literal: Seventh: Zheng music confounds Ya music.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, popular Zheng music was corrupting the courtly Ya repertoire.

sentences.zh: 然朱紫有色而易別，雅、鄭無象而難知，聖人懼其難知也，故定律呂中正之音，以示萬世。

translations.literal: Yet red and purple have color and are easy to distinguish; Ya and Zheng have no image and are hard to know; the sage feared their being hard to know, and therefore established the correct tones of the pitch pipes to show ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson and purple are visible colors and easy to tell apart, but Ya and Zheng leave no outward mark and are hard to recognize. The sages feared that difficulty, and so they fixed the correct pitches of the pipes as a standard for all later ages.

sentences.zh: 今古器尚存，律呂悉備，而學士、大夫不講考擊，奏作委之賤工，則雅、鄭不得不雜。

translations.literal: Now the ancient instruments still exist, and the pitch pipes are all complete, yet scholars and grandees do not discuss striking and examining them, and entrust performance to base craftsmen—then Ya and Zheng must be mixed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient instruments still survive and the full set of pipes remains, yet literati and officials no longer study how to strike and test them, leaving performance to lowly artisans. Under such conditions Ya and Zheng cannot help but mingle.

sentences.zh: 願審調鍾琯用十二律還宮均法，令上下通習，則鄭聲莫能亂雅。

translations.literal: It is wished that the tuning of bells and pitch tubes use the twelve-pitch returning-to-the-palace equalization method, and order those above and below to practice it thoroughly—then Zheng music could not confound Ya.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that bell and pipe tuning follow the twelve-pitch 'return to the palace' method and that everyone from the court down be trained in it, so that Zheng music could no longer corrupt Ya.

sentences.zh: 遂為十二均圖，並上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made a diagram of the twelve keys and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore drew a chart of the twelve keys and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其論以為：“律各有均，有七聲，更相為用。

translations.literal: His discourse held that: 'Each pitch pipe has its key; there are seven tones, mutually used in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: In his argument he wrote: 'Each pitch standard has its own key. There are seven tones that may be used in turn with one another.

sentences.zh: 協本均則樂調，非本均則樂悖。

translations.literal: When the fundamental key is coordinated, the music is in tune; when it is not the fundamental key, the music is perverse.
translations.idiomatic: When performance stays on the fundamental key, the music is true; when it departs from that key, the music turns false.

sentences.zh: 今黃鍾為宮，則太簇、姑洗、林鍾、南呂、應鍾、蕤賓七聲相應，謂之黃鍾之均。

translations.literal: Now if Yellow Bell is taken as the palace tone, then Great Cou, Gu Xian, Forest Bell, Southern Lu, Responding Bell, and Flanking Guest—the seven tones—respond, and this is called the Yellow Bell key.
translations.idiomatic: If Yellow Bell serves as the palace tone, then Great Cou, Gu Xian, Forest Bell, Southern Lu, Responding Bell, and Flanking Guest—the seven tones—answer it. That combination is called the Yellow Bell key.

sentences.zh: 餘律為宮，同之。

translations.literal: Taking the remaining pitch pipes as palace tones is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle applies when any of the other pitches is taken as palace tone.

sentences.zh: 宮為君，商為臣，角為民，徵為事，羽為物。

translations.literal: Palace is the ruler, Shang is the minister, Jue is the people, Zhi is affairs, and Yu is things.
translations.idiomatic: Palace stands for the ruler, Shang for the minister, Jue for the people, Zhi for affairs, and Yu for things.

sentences.zh: 君者，法度號令之所出，故宮生徵；

translations.literal: The ruler is where law, standards, and commands issue forth; therefore palace generates zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the source of law, measure, and command; therefore palace generates zhi.

sentences.zh: 法度號令所以授臣而承行之，故徽生商；

translations.literal: Law, standards, and commands are what are conferred on ministers to receive and carry out; therefore zhi generates shang.
translations.idiomatic: Law and command are handed to ministers to receive and execute; therefore zhi generates shang.

sentences.zh: 君臣一德，以康庶事，則萬物得所，民遂其生，故商生羽，羽生角。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister share one virtue to bring the myriad affairs to peace; then the myriad things obtain their places, the people follow their livelihoods—therefore shang generates yu, and yu generates jue.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister share one virtue and the myriad affairs are well ordered, the myriad things find their place and the people secure their livelihoods; therefore shang generates yu, and yu generates jue.

sentences.zh: 然臣有常職，民有常業，物有常形，而遷則失常，故商、角、羽無變聲。

translations.literal: Yet ministers have constant duties, people have constant occupations, things have constant forms, and if they shift then they lose the constant; therefore shang, jue, and yu have no changing tones.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers have fixed offices, people fixed trades, and things fixed forms; change would mean losing what is constant. Hence shang, jue, and yu have no altered tones.

sentences.zh: 君總萬化，不可執以一方；

translations.literal: The ruler presides over the myriad transformations and cannot be fixed to one side.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler oversees the myriad transformations and cannot be confined to a single mode.

sentences.zh: 事通萬務，不可滯於一隅：故宮、徵有變聲。

translations.literal: Affairs penetrate the myriad tasks and cannot stagnate in one corner: therefore palace and zhi have changing tones.
translations.idiomatic: Public business touches every task and cannot be stuck in one corner; therefore palace and zhi admit altered tones.

sentences.zh: 凡律呂之調及其宮、樂章，具著於圖。”

translations.literal: All the tunings of the pitch pipes and their palace tones and music sections are fully set forth in the diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Every pitch tuning, its palace tone, and its musical sections are laid out in full in the chart.

sentences.zh: 帝取所上圖，考其說，乃下鎮、幾參定。

translations.literal: The emperor took the submitted diagram, examined the discourse, and thereupon ordered Zhen and Ji to deliberate and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied the chart and its argument, then directed Fan Zhen and Liu Ji to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 而王樸、阮逸之黃鍾乃當李照之太簇，其編鍾、編磬雖有四清聲，而黃鍾、大呂正聲舛誤；

translations.literal: Yet Wang Pu's and Ruan Yi's Yellow Bell was equivalent to Li Zhao's Great Cou; their arranged bells and chime-stones, though they had the four clear tones, had Yellow Bell and Great Lu fundamental tones in error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yellow Bell of Wang Pu and Ruan Yi matched Li Zhao's Great Cou in pitch. Their serial bells and chimes included the four clear tones, but the fundamental Yellow Bell and Great Lu were wrong.

sentences.zh: 照之編鍾、編磬雖有黃鍾、大呂，而全闕四清聲，非古製也。

translations.literal: Zhao's arranged bells and chime-stones, though they had Yellow Bell and Great Lu, entirely lacked the four clear tones—this is not the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao's serial bells and chimes had Yellow Bell and Great Lu but omitted the four clear tones entirely—again departing from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 樸之太簇、夾鍾，則聲失之高，歌者莫能追逐，平時設而不用。

translations.literal: Pu's Great Cou and Flanking Guest then had sounds that erred on the high side, and singers could not pursue them; they were set out in ordinary times but not used.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's Great Cou and Flanking Guest ran too high for singers to follow and were kept on hand but never played in regular service.

sentences.zh: 聖人作樂以紀中和之聲，所以導中和之氣，清不可太高，重不可太下，必使八音協諧、歌者從容而能永其言。

translations.literal: The sage made music to record the sound of central harmony, thereby to guide the qi of central harmony; the clear cannot be too high, the heavy cannot be too low—one must make the eight tones harmonize and singers be at ease so they can prolong their words.
translations.idiomatic: The sages fashioned music to embody balanced sound and thereby to cultivate balanced breath. Clarity must not rise too high, nor weight sink too low; the eight categories of tone must blend, and singers must be able to sustain the text at ease.

sentences.zh: 鎮等因請擇李照編鍾、編磬十二參於律者，增以王樸無射、應鍾及黃鍾、大呂清聲，以為黃鍾、大呂、太簇、夾鍾之四清聲，俾眾樂隨之，歌工詠之，中和之聲庶可以考。

translations.literal: Zhen and the others therefore requested to select from Li Zhao's arranged bells and chime-stones the twelve that accorded with the pitch pipes, add Wang Pu's Wushe and Responding Bell and the clear tones of Yellow Bell and Great Lu as the four clear tones of Yellow Bell, Great Lu, Great Cou, and Flanking Guest, so that all music would follow them and singing workers would chant to them—then the sound of central harmony might be examined.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen and his colleagues therefore proposed taking the twelve of Li Zhao's serial bells and chimes that matched the standard pitches, adding Wang Pu's Wushe and Responding Bell plus the clear variants of Yellow Bell and Great Lu to form the four clear tones of Yellow Bell, Great Lu, Great Cou, and Flanking Guest, so that the whole orchestra and the choristers could follow them and the balanced sound might finally be tested.

sentences.zh: 請下樸二律。

translations.literal: They requested to remove Pu's two pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that Pu's two pitches be taken down.

sentences.zh: 就太常鍾磬擇其可用者用之，其不可修者別製之。

translations.literal: From the bells and chime-stones of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, select those that can be used and use them; those that cannot be repaired, manufacture separately.
translations.idiomatic: Among the bells and stones already in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, they should use what could still serve and replace what could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 而太常以為大樂法度舊器，乞留樸鍾磬，別製新樂，以驗議者之術。

translations.literal: But the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that the great music's standards and old instruments should be kept, and begged to retain Pu's bells and chime-stones and manufacture new music separately, to test the proponents' methods.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices, however, argued that the great music's canonical instruments should be preserved. They asked to keep Pu's bells and stones and build a new set beside them so the reformers' methods could be tried without destroying the old standard.

sentences.zh: 詔以樸樂鍾為清聲，毋得銷毀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Pu's music bells be kept as clear tones and must not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that Pu's bells be preserved as clear-tone instruments and not destroyed.

sentences.zh: 幾等謂：“新樂之成，足以薦郊廟，傳萬世。

translations.literal: Ji and the others said: 'The completion of the new music is sufficient to offer at the suburban altars and be transmitted for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and his colleagues said: 'Once the new music is finished, it will suffice for the suburban sacrifices and endure for ages.

sentences.zh: 其明堂、景靈宮降天神之樂六奏：舊用夾鍾之均三奏，謂之夾鍾為宮；

translations.literal: Its music for descending the Heavenly Spirit at the Bright Hall and Jingling Palace has six presentations: formerly using the Flanking Guest key for three presentations, called taking Flanking Guest as palace.
translations.idiomatic: The six movements that summon the Heavenly Spirit at the Bright Hall and Jingling Palace formerly used the Flanking Guest key for three sections, called 'Flanking Guest as palace.'

sentences.zh: 夷則之均一奏，謂之黃鍾為角；

translations.literal: The Yize key for one presentation, called taking Yellow Bell as jue.
translations.idiomatic: One section used the Yize key, called 'Yellow Bell as jue.'

sentences.zh: 林鍾之均一奏，謂之太簇為徵。

translations.literal: The Forest Bell key for one presentation, called taking Great Cou as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: One section used the Forest Bell key, called 'Great Cou as zhi.'

sentences.zh: 姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Gu Xian as yu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xian served as yu.

sentences.zh: 而《大司樂》‘凡樂，圜鍾為宮，黃鍾為角，太簇為徵，姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Yet the Grand Music Master states: 'For all music, Round Bell is palace, Yellow Bell is jue, Great Cou is zhi, Gu Xian is yu.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Grand Music Master says: 'In all music, Round Bell is palace, Yellow Bell is jue, Great Cou is zhi, and Gu Xian is yu.'

sentences.zh: ’而‘圜鍾者，夾鍾也’。

translations.literal: And 'Round Bell is Flanking Guest.'
translations.idiomatic: And 'Round Bell is Flanking Guest.'

sentences.zh: 用夾鍾均之七聲，以其宮聲為始終，是謂圜鍾為宮；

translations.literal: Using the seven tones of the Flanking Guest key, taking its palace tone as beginning and end—this is called Round Bell as palace.
translations.idiomatic: To use the seven tones of the Flanking Guest key with its palace tone as beginning and end is what is meant by 'Round Bell as palace.'

sentences.zh: 用黃鍾均之七聲，以其角聲為始終，是謂黃鍾為角；

translations.literal: Using the seven tones of the Yellow Bell key, taking its jue tone as beginning and end—this is called Yellow Bell as jue.
translations.idiomatic: To use the seven tones of the Yellow Bell key with its jue tone as beginning and end is what is meant by 'Yellow Bell as jue.'

sentences.zh: 用太簇均之七聲，以其徵聲為始終，是謂太簇為徵；

translations.literal: Using the seven tones of the Great Cou key, taking its zhi tone as beginning and end—this is called Great Cou as zhi.
translations.idiomatic: To use the seven tones of the Great Cou key with its zhi tone as beginning and end is what is meant by 'Great Cou as zhi.'

sentences.zh: 用姑洗均之七聲，以其羽聲為始終，是謂姑洗為羽。

translations.literal: Using the seven tones of the Gu Xian key, taking its yu tone as beginning and end—this is called Gu Xian as yu.
translations.idiomatic: To use the seven tones of the Gu Xian key with its yu tone as beginning and end is what is meant by 'Gu Xian as yu.'

sentences.zh: 今用夷則之均一奏，謂之黃鍾為角，林鍾之均二奏，謂之太簇為徵、姑洗為羽，則祀天之樂無夷則、林鍾而用之，有太簇、姑洗而去之矣。

translations.literal: Now using the Yize key for one presentation, called Yellow Bell as jue, and the Forest Bell key for two presentations, called Great Cou as zhi and Gu Xian as yu—then in the music for sacrificing to Heaven there are no Yize or Forest Bell used, while Great Cou and Gu Xian are present yet removed.
translations.idiomatic: But if one section is performed in the Yize key as 'Yellow Bell as jue' and two in the Forest Bell key as 'Great Cou as zhi' and 'Gu Xian as yu,' then the music for Heaven's sacrifice employs Yize and Forest Bell while omitting the very Great Cou and Gu Xian the rites require.

sentences.zh: 唐典，祀天以夾鍾宮、黃鍾角、太簇徵、姑洗羽，乃周禮也，宜用夾鍾為宮。

translations.literal: The Tang code, in sacrificing to Heaven used Flanking Guest palace, Yellow Bell jue, Great Cou zhi, Gu Xian yu—this is the Zhou rites, and Flanking Guest should be used as palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang regulations for the sacrifice to Heaven used Flanking Guest as palace, Yellow Bell as jue, Great Cou as zhi, and Gu Xian as yu—the Zhou arrangement—and Flanking Guest should therefore serve as palace.

sentences.zh: 其黃鍾為角，則用黃鍾均，以其角聲為始終；

translations.literal: For Yellow Bell as jue, then use the Yellow Bell key, taking its jue tone as beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: For 'Yellow Bell as jue,' one should use the Yellow Bell key with its jue tone as beginning and end.

sentences.zh: 太簇為徵，則用太簇均，以其徵聲為始終；

translations.literal: For Great Cou as zhi, then use the Great Cou key, taking its zhi tone as beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: For 'Great Cou as zhi,' one should use the Great Cou key with its zhi tone as beginning and end.

sentences.zh: 姑洗為羽，則用姑洗均，以其羽聲為始終。

translations.literal: For Gu Xian as yu, then use the Gu Xian key, taking its yu tone as beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: For 'Gu Xian as yu,' one should use the Gu Xian key with its yu tone as beginning and end.

sentences.zh: 祭地祇，享宗廟，皆視此均法以度曲。”

translations.literal: Sacrifices to the earthly spirits and feasts in the ancestral temple all take this key method to measure the melodies.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices to Earth and the ancestral feasts should all set their melodies by this same key method.

sentences.zh: 幾等又以太常磬三等，王樸磬厚，李照磬薄，惟阮逸、胡瑗磬形製精密而聲太高，以磬氏之法摩其旁，輕重與律呂相應。

translations.literal: Ji and the others also took the three grades of chime-stones in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: Wang Pu's chime-stones were thick, Li Zhao's thin; only Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's chime-stones were precise in form yet their sound was too high—using the chime-maker's method they filed the sides so that weight and lightness corresponded to the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and his colleagues also compared the Court's three grades of stone chimes: Wang Pu's were thick, Li Zhao's thin, while only Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's were finely shaped yet pitched too high. They filed the sides by the chime-makers' method until weight and pitch matched the standard pipes.

sentences.zh: 鍾三等，王樸鍾所謂“聲疾而短聞”者也，阮逸、胡瑗鍾所謂“聲舒而遠聞”者也，惟李照鍾有旋蟲之製。

translations.literal: The bells had three grades: Wang Pu's bells were what is called 'sound swift and short in hearing'; Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's bells were what is called 'sound leisurely and far in hearing'; only Li Zhao's bells had the rotating-worm mechanism.
translations.idiomatic: The bells likewise fell into three types: Wang Pu's were said to sound quick and fade soon; Ruan Yi and Hu Yuan's sounded slow and carried far; only Li Zhao's bells bore the adjustable worm mechanism.

sentences.zh: 鍾磬皆三十有六架，架各十有六，則正律相應，清聲自足。

translations.literal: Bells and chime-stones each had thirty-six frames; each frame had sixteen pieces, so the fundamental pitch pipes responded and the clear tones were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and stones were set on thirty-six frames of sixteen pieces each, so the root pitches answered one another and the clear subsidiary tones were complete.

sentences.zh: 其堂上堂下篪、笛率從新製，而調琴、瑟、阮、築、塤諸器，隨所下律。

translations.literal: The chi and vertical flutes above and below the hall mostly followed the new manufacture, while the qin, se, ruan, zhu, and ocarina were tuned to whatever pitch pipes were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Hall and courtyard chi and flutes were largely remade to the new standard, while zithers, harps, ruan, zhu, and ocarinas were tuned to the newly fixed pitches.

sentences.zh: 詔悉從之。

translations.literal: An edict fully approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 乃緝新器用，徙置太常，辟屋以貯藏之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered the new instruments for use, moved them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and opened rooms to store them.
translations.idiomatic: They then assembled the new instruments, transferred them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and set aside storehouses for them.

sentences.zh: 考選樂工，汰其椎鈍癃老，而優募能者補其闕員，立為程度，以時習焉。

translations.literal: They examined and selected music workers, eliminated the dull, aged, and infirm, and generously recruited the able to fill the vacancies, establishing standards and practicing them on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians were examined, the dull and aged dismissed, skilled recruits enlisted to fill gaps, and regular training schedules established.

sentences.zh: 初，皇祐中，益州進士房庶論尺律之法，以為嚐得古本《漢書》，言在《律曆志》。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Huangyou era, the licentiate Fang Shu of Yizhou discoursed on the method of pitch pipes and measures, holding that he had once obtained an ancient edition of the Book of Han stating it was in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Huangyou, the Yizhou graduate Fang Shu argued for a method of pitch pipes and measures, claiming he had found an old Han shu passage in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 範鎮以其說為然，請依法作為尺律，然後別求古樂參考。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen held his discourse to be correct and requested that pitch pipes and measures be made according to the law, and only then separately seek ancient music for reference.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen accepted Fang Shu's account and asked that pipes and measures be cast by that method before ancient music was sought for comparison.

sentences.zh: 於是庶奉詔造律管二，尺、量、龠各一，而殿中丞胡瑗以為非。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu received an edict to manufacture two pitch pipes, and one each of measure, capacity vessel, and yue; but the Palace Aide Hu Yuan held it was not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shu was ordered to make two pitch pipes plus a ruler, a measure, and a yue vessel, while Palace Aide Hu Yuan objected that the method was wrong.

sentences.zh: 詔鎮與幾等定樂，鎮曰：“定樂當先正律。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhen and Ji and others to fix the music; Zhen said: 'To fix music one must first correct the pitch pipes.'
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhen and Liu Ji were charged with fixing the music, Zhen said, 'Music cannot be settled until the pitch standards are corrected.'

sentences.zh: ”帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 鎮作律、尺等，欲圖上之。

translations.literal: Zhen made pitch pipes, measures, and the like, and wished to submit diagrams of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen fashioned pipes, measures, and related tools and prepared to present diagrams of them.

sentences.zh: 而幾之議律主於人聲，不以尺度求合。

translations.literal: But Ji's discourse on pitch pipes took the human voice as its basis and did not seek agreement through measures and scales.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, however, grounded pitch on the human voice and refused to force it to match physical measures.

sentences.zh: 其樂大抵即李照之舊而加四清聲，遂奏樂成。

translations.literal: His music was mostly Li Zhao's old system with the four clear tones added; thereupon they presented that the music was complete.
translations.idiomatic: His music was essentially Li Zhao's old arrangement with the four clear tones restored, and he reported the work finished.

sentences.zh: 第加恩賚，而鎮謝曰：“此劉幾樂也，臣何預焉！

translations.literal: He was only to receive favor and reward, but Zhen declined, saying: 'This is Liu Ji's music—how should your servant have a part in it!'
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were offered, Fan Zhen declined: 'This is Liu Ji's music. What part had I in it?'

sentences.zh: ”乃復上奏曰：“太常鎛鍾皆有大小、輕重之法，非三代莫能為者。

translations.literal: He then again submitted a memorial saying: 'The great bells of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices all have methods of large and small, heavy and light—none but the Three Dynasties could make them.'
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized again: 'The Court's great bells follow rules of size and weight that only the Three Dynasties could truly execute.'

sentences.zh: 禁中又出李照、胡瑗所鑄銅律及尺付太常，按照黃鍾律合王樸太簇律，仲呂律合王樸黃鍾律，比樸樂才下半律，外有損益而內無損益，鍾聲鬱而不發，無足議者。

translations.literal: The inner palace also issued the copper pitch pipes and measures cast by Li Zhao and Hu Yuan to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; comparing Yellow Bell pipe with Wang Pu's Great Cou pipe and Zhonglu pipe with Wang Pu's Yellow Bell pipe, they were only half a pitch lower than Pu's music; outwardly there were additions and subtractions but inwardly none—the bell sound was muffled and did not issue, not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The palace also sent Li Zhao and Hu Yuan's bronze pipes and measures to the Court. Yellow Bell under their system matched Wang Pu's Great Cou, and Zhonglu matched Wang Pu's Yellow Bell—only half a pitch below Pu's scale. Outwardly the numbers shifted, inwardly they did not; the bells sounded choked and were not worth debating.

sentences.zh: 照之律雖是，然與其樂校，三格自相違戾。

translations.literal: Zhao's pitch pipes were correct in themselves, yet when compared with his music, the three modes mutually contradicted one another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao's pipes might be right in theory, yet compared with his music the three modes contradicted one another.

sentences.zh: 且以太簇為黃鍾，則是商為宮也。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking Great Cou as Yellow Bell means taking Shang as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to call Great Cou Yellow Bell is to make Shang the palace tone.

sentences.zh: 方劉幾奏上時，臣初無所預。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji submitted his work, your servant had no part in it at first.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji first presented his music, I had no hand in it.

sentences.zh: 臣頃造律，內外有損益，其聲和，又與古樂合。

translations.literal: Your servant recently made pitch pipes; inwardly and outwardly there were additions and subtractions, yet their sound was harmonious and again matched ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: The pipes I have lately made adjust inner and outer dimensions, yet sound harmoniously and accord with ancient music.

sentences.zh: 今若將臣所造尺律依大小編次太常鎛鍾，可以成一代大典。

translations.literal: Now if my pitch pipes and measures are arranged in order of size on the Court's great bells, a great canonical music for the age can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: If my pipes and measures were used to rank the Court's great bells by size, the dynasty could possess a true canonical music.

sentences.zh: 又太常無雷鼓、靈鼓、路鼓，而以散鼓代之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Court of Imperial Sacrifices has no thunder drum, spirit drum, or road drum, but uses the loose drum in their place.
translations.idiomatic: The Court also lacks the thunder, spirit, and road drums, substituting ordinary hand drums.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有以畫圖獻者，一鼓而為八面、六面、四面，明皇用之。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era someone presented a painted diagram in which one drum had eight faces, six faces, or four faces, and Emperor Ming used it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan someone offered a painted diagram of drums with eight, six, or four faces, and Emperor Xuanzong adopted it.

sentences.zh: 國朝郊廟或考或不考，宮架中惟以散鼓，不應經義。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's suburban and temple rites it is sometimes followed and sometimes not; in the palace orchestra only the loose drum is used, which does not accord with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Our suburban and temple rites sometimes follow that practice and sometimes do not; the palace orchestra relies solely on the loose drum, which the classics do not sanction.

sentences.zh: 又八音無匏、土二音：笙、竽以木鬥攢竹而以匏裹之，是無匏音也；

translations.literal: Moreover the eight tones lack the two of gourd and earth: the sheng and yu use wooden sockets to gather bamboo and are wrapped with gourd—thus there is no gourd tone.
translations.idiomatic: The eight categories also lack true gourd and earth tones: sheng and yu bind bamboo in wooden frames wrapped with gourd, so no true gourd tone remains.

sentences.zh: 塤器以木為之，是無土音也。

translations.literal: The ocarina is made of wood—thus there is no earth tone.
translations.idiomatic: The ocarina is made of wood, so there is no true earth tone either.

sentences.zh: 八音不具，以為備樂，安可得哉！

translations.literal: The eight tones are not complete—how can this be considered complete music!
translations.idiomatic: With the eight tones incomplete, how can this count as full ritual music?

sentences.zh: ”不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，詳定所言：“‘搏拊、琴、瑟以詠’，則堂上之樂，以象朝廷之治；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, the deliberation office stated: ''Beating clappers, qin, and se to chant'—thus the music above the hall images the governance of the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanfeng, the deliberation office wrote: 'The line about clappers, zithers, and harps for chanting describes hall music imaging court governance.'

sentences.zh: ‘下管、鞀鼓’，‘合止敔’，‘笙、鏞以間’，則堂下之樂，以象萬物之治。

translations.literal: 'Lower pipes and hand drums,' 'combine and stop with the wooden clapper,' 'sheng and yong to intersperse'—thus the music below the hall images the governance of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lower pipes and hand drums,' 'uniting and closing with the clapper,' and 'sheng and yong interspersed' describe courtyard music imaging the ordering of the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 後世有司失其傳，歌者在堂，兼設鍾磬；

translations.literal: Later officials lost the transmission; singers are in the hall while bells and chime-stones are also set up.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials lost the tradition: singers stand in the hall while bells and chimes are placed there as well.

sentences.zh: 宮架在庭，兼設琴瑟；

translations.literal: The palace orchestra is in the courtyard while qin and se are also set up.
translations.idiomatic: The palace orchestra stands in the courtyard while zithers and harps are set up there too.

sentences.zh: 堂下匏竹，寘之於床：並非其序。

translations.literal: Gourd and bamboo below the hall are placed on beds—all not in their proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd and bamboo instruments below the hall are set on platforms—all out of proper order.

sentences.zh: 請親祠宗廟及有司攝事，歌者在堂，不設鍾磬；

translations.literal: It is requested that for the emperor's personal sacrifices in the ancestral temple and for officials' proxy rites, singers be in the hall and bells and chime-stones not be set up.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that at the emperor's own temple sacrifices and at proxy rites, singers remain in the hall without bells or chimes.

sentences.zh: 宮架在庭，不設琴瑟；

translations.literal: The palace orchestra be in the courtyard and qin and se not be set up.
translations.idiomatic: The palace orchestra should stay in the courtyard without zithers or harps.

sentences.zh: 堂下匏竹，不寘於床。

translations.literal: Gourd and bamboo below the hall not be placed on beds.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd and bamboo below the hall should not be placed on platforms.

sentences.zh: 其郊壇上下之樂，亦以此為正，而有司攝事如之。

translations.literal: The music above and below the suburban altars should also take this as correct, and officials' proxy rites should follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altar music above and below should follow the same rule, as should proxy rites.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“以《小胥》宮縣推之，則天子鍾、磬、鎛十二虡為宮縣明矣。

translations.literal: They also stated: 'Deducing from the Palace Music Master of the Small Steward, then the Son of Heaven's bells, chime-stones, and great bells in twelve frames for the palace orchestra is clear.'
translations.idiomatic: They also argued from the Small Steward's account of the palace orchestra that the Son of Heaven's bells, stones, and great bells in twelve frames were clearly defined.

sentences.zh: 故或以為配十二辰，或以為配十二次，則虡無過十二。

translations.literal: Therefore some hold that they match the twelve chronograms, or match the twelve stations of the zodiac—then frames should not exceed twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Some therefore paired them with the twelve chronograms or the twelve lunar lodges, so frames should not exceed twelve.

sentences.zh: 先王之製廢，學者不能考其數。

translations.literal: The former kings' system was abandoned, and scholars could not investigate the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ancient system fell away, scholars could no longer recover the numbers.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐以來，有謂宮縣當二十虡，甚者又以為三十六虡。

translations.literal: From Sui and Tang onward, some said the palace orchestra should have twenty frames, and some even said thirty-six frames.
translations.idiomatic: From Sui and Tang some claimed twenty frames for the palace orchestra, and others as many as thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 方唐之盛日，有司攝事，樂並用宮縣。

translations.literal: In the flourishing days of Tang, when officials performed proxy rites, music all used the palace orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: At Tang's height, proxy sacrifices still employed the full palace orchestra.

sentences.zh: 至德後，太常聲音之工散亡，凡郊廟有登歌而無宮縣，後世因仍不改。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, the sound craftsmen of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices scattered and were lost; for suburban and temple rites there was ascending song but no palace orchestra, and later ages followed this without change.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide, Court musicians dispersed; suburban and temple rites retained ascending song but lost the palace orchestra, and later ages never restored it.

sentences.zh: 請郊廟有司攝事，改用宮架十二虡。

translations.literal: It is requested that for suburban and temple proxy rites, the palace orchestra of twelve frames be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that proxy suburban and temple rites again use the twelve-frame palace orchestra.

sentences.zh: ”太常以謂用宮架十二虡，則律呂均聲不足，不能成均。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that if the palace orchestra used twelve frames, the pitch pipes' equal tones would be insufficient and could not form the complete scale.
translations.idiomatic: The Court objected that twelve frames would leave the pitch pipes' full scale incomplete.

sentences.zh: 請如禮：宮架四面如辰位，設鎛鍾十二虡，而甲、丙、庚、壬設鍾，乙、丁、辛、癸設磬，位各一虡。

translations.literal: It is requested to follow the rites: the palace orchestra on four sides like the chronogram positions, setting twelve frames of great bells, with jia, bing, geng, and ren setting bells and yi, ding, xin, and gui setting chime-stones, one frame at each position.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed instead the ritual layout: orchestra on four sides like the chronogram stations, twelve frames of great bells, bells on jia, bing, geng, and ren and chimes on yi, ding, xin, and gui, one frame each.

sentences.zh: 四隅植建鼓，以象二十四氣。

translations.literal: At the four corners erect mounted drums to image the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted drums at the four corners would image the twenty-four seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 宗廟、郊丘如之。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple and suburban mound rites would follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Temple and suburban rites would follow the same plan.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，開封布衣葉防上書論樂器、律曲不應古法，復下楊傑議。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Ye Fang, a commoner of Kaifeng, submitted a memorial discussing that instruments and pitch melodies did not accord with ancient law, and again Yang Jie was ordered to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, the Kaifeng commoner Ye Fang memorialized that instruments and melodies no longer matched antiquity, and Yang Jie was again ordered to respond.

sentences.zh: 傑論防增編鍾、編磬二十有四為簨製，管簫視鍾磬數，登歌用玉磬，去樂曲之近清聲者，舞不立表，皆非是。

translations.literal: Jie discussed that Fang's proposals to increase arranged bells and chime-stones to twenty-four in bamboo-casket frames, make pan-pipes and vertical flutes match the number of bells and chimes, use jade chime-stones for ascending song, remove melodies' near-clear tones, and not set up markers for dance were all wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jie rejected Fang's plan to raise serial bells and chimes to twenty-four in casket frames, match flutes to bell counts, use jade chimes for ascending song, drop near-clear tones, and abolish dance markers.

sentences.zh: 其言均律差互，與劉幾同。

translations.literal: His words on equal pitch pipes being mutually contradictory were the same as Liu Ji's.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's complaints about conflicting pitch standards echoed Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 請以晉鼓節金奏。

translations.literal: It is requested to use the Jin drum to mark the metal performance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Jin drum mark the metal percussion.

sentences.zh: 考經、禮，製簨虡教國子、宗子舞，用之郊廟，為何所取？

translations.literal: Examining the classics and rites, making bamboo frames to teach the sons of the state and imperial clansmen to dance and using them at suburban altars and temples—what is this taken from?
translations.idiomatic: By what classical warrant were bamboo frames to train princes and clansmen in dance, then used at suburban and temple rites?

sentences.zh: 而範鎮亦言：“自唐以來至國朝，三大祀樂譜並依《周禮》，然其說有黃鍾為角、黃鍾之角。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen also said: 'From Tang down to our dynasty, the music scores for the three great sacrifices all follow the Rites of Zhou, yet the explanations have Yellow Bell as jue and Yellow Bell's jue.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen added: 'From Tang through our dynasty the three great sacrifices followed the Zhou Rites, yet commentators speak of both Yellow Bell as jue and Yellow Bell's jue.'

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為角者，夷則為宮；

translations.literal: Yellow Bell as jue means Yize is palace.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yellow Bell as jue' means Yize serves as palace.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾之角者，姑洗為角。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell's jue means Gu Xian is jue.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yellow Bell's jue' means Gu Xian is jue.

sentences.zh: 十二律之於五聲，皆如此率。

translations.literal: The twelve pitch pipes in relation to the five tones are all like this in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle governs all twelve pipes against the five tones.

sentences.zh: 而世俗之說，乃去‘之’字，謂太簇曰黃鍾商，姑洗曰黃鍾角，林鍾曰黃鍾徵，南呂曰黃鍾羽。

translations.literal: Yet vulgar explanations omit the word 'of' and say Great Cou is Yellow Bell shang, Gu Xian is Yellow Bell jue, Forest Bell is Yellow Bell zhi, Southern Lu is Yellow Bell yu.
translations.idiomatic: Popular usage drops the possessive and calls Great Cou 'Yellow Bell shang,' Gu Xian 'Yellow Bell jue,' Forest Bell 'Yellow Bell zhi,' and Southern Lu 'Yellow Bell yu.'

sentences.zh: 今葉防但通世俗夷部之說，而不見《周禮》正文，所以稱本寺均差互，其說難行。

translations.literal: Now Ye Fang onlyfollows the vulgar Yize-section explanations and does not see the correct text of the Rites of Zhou; therefore he says this office's keys are mutually contradictory and his proposals are hard to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Fang follows only popular Yize-key formulas and ignores the Zhou Rites themselves, which is why he finds the Court's keys contradictory and his plan unworkable.

sentences.zh: ”帝以樂律絕學，防草萊中習之尤難，乃補防為樂正。

translations.literal: The emperor, because music and pitch learning had died out and it was especially hard for Fang to study it as a commoner in the fields, nevertheless appointed Fang as Director of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Because pitch theory had nearly vanished, the emperor admired that a farmer had mastered it and appointed Ye Fang Director of Music.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，禦大慶殿，初用新樂。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the sixth year, the emperor proceeded to the Great Celebration Hall and for the first time used the new music.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng the emperor entered the Great Celebration Hall and performed with the new music for the first time.

sentences.zh: 二月，太常言：“郊廟樂虡，若遇雨雪，望祭即設於殿上。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: 'Suburban and temple music frames, if rain or snow occurs, are set up in the hall for the observance sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Court reported that when rain or snow fell, suburban music frames could be set up in the hall for the observance sacrifice.

sentences.zh: ”三月，禮部言：“有司攝事，祀昊天舞名。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Ministry of Rites stated: 'For officials' proxy rites, the dance name for sacrificing to August Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Ministry of Rites proposed dance titles for proxy sacrifices to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請初獻曰《帝臨嘉至》，亞、終獻曰《神矣錫羨》；

translations.literal: It is requested that the first offering be called 'The Emperor Approaches in Blessing,' and the second and final offerings be called 'The Spirit Bestows Favor.'
translations.idiomatic: The first offering dance should be called 'The Emperor Approaches in Blessing,' the second and final 'The Spirit Bestows Favor.'

sentences.zh: 太廟初獻曰《孝熙昭德》，亞、終獻曰《禮洽儲祥》。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple first offering: 'Filial Splendor and Bright Virtue'; second and final offerings: 'Rites Harmonize and Store Blessings.'
translations.idiomatic: For the Imperial Ancestral Temple: first offering 'Filial Splendor and Bright Virtue,' second and final 'Rites Harmonize and Store Blessings.'

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 九月，禮部言：“《周禮》，凡大祭祀，王出入則奏《王夏》，明入廟門已用樂矣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Ministry of Rites stated: 'The Rites of Zhou: for all great sacrifices, when the king enters and exits, the Wang Xia is played—clearly music was already used upon entering the temple gate.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Ministry cited the Zhou Rites: at great sacrifices the king's entry and exit were accompanied by 'Wang Xia,' showing music began at the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 今既移祼在作樂之前，皇帝詣罍洗奏《乾安》，則入門亦當奏《乾安》，庶合古製。

translations.literal: Now since the libation has been moved before the music begins, when the emperor reaches the libation ewer the Qian An is played; then upon entering the gate Qian An should also be played, so as to accord with the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Because libation now precedes the main music, 'Qian An' plays at the libation ewer; they asked that 'Qian An' also play at the gate to match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其入景靈宮及南郊壝門，乞如之。”

translations.literal: For entering Jingling Palace and the southern suburban mound gate, it is requested to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The same should apply on entering Jingling Palace and the southern suburban mound gate.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，詔從協律郎榮谘道請，於奉宸庫選玉造磬，令太常審定音律。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, an edict followed the request of the Pitch-Matching Officer Rong Zidao to select jade from the Imperial Treasury to make chime-stones and order the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to determine the pitch.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year of Yuanfeng the throne approved Pitch-Matching Officer Rong Zidao's request to choose jade from the Imperial Treasury for chimes and have the Court fix the pitch.

sentences.zh: 六月，禮部言：“親郊之歲，夏至祀皇地祇於方丘，遣塚宰攝事，禮容樂舞謂宜加於常祀。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Ministry of Rites stated: 'In a year when the emperor personally performs the suburban sacrifice, at the summer solstice August Earth is sacrificed at the square mound; the chief minister performs the proxy rite, and the ritual bearing and music and dance should be greater than the regular sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Ministry noted that in years of the emperor's personal suburban sacrifice, the summer solstice Earth rite at the square mound, though performed by the chief minister as proxy, should exceed ordinary proxy rites in ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 而其樂虡二十、樂工百五十有二、舞者六十有四，與常歲南北郊上公攝事無異，未足以稱欽崇之意。

translations.literal: Yet its music frames are twenty, music workers one hundred fifty-two, and dancers sixty-four—the same as when a chief minister performs the regular southern and northern suburban proxy rites in ordinary years, insufficient to express reverent esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it still used only twenty frames, 152 musicians, and 64 dancers—the same as an ordinary chief-minister proxy sacrifice—too meager to express full reverence.

sentences.zh: 乞自今準親祠用三十六虡，工人三百有六，舞人百二十有四。

translations.literal: From now on it is requested to follow the personal sacrifice standard of thirty-six frames, three hundred six workers, and one hundred twenty-four dancers.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that henceforth it follow the imperial standard: thirty-six frames, 306 musicians, and 124 dancers.

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，谘道又言：“先帝詔臣製造玉磬，將用於廟堂之上，依舊同編鍾以登歌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Zidao again stated: 'The former emperor ordered your servant to manufacture jade chime-stones to be used in the temple hall above, following the old practice of pairing them with arranged bells for ascending song.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1, Zidao again reported that the late emperor had ordered him to make jade chimes for the temple hall, paired with serial bells for ascending song as of old.

sentences.zh: 今年親祠明堂，請用之，以章明盛典。

translations.literal: This year's personal sacrifice at the Bright Hall—please use them to display the brilliance of the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to use them at this year's personal Bright Hall sacrifice to honor the grand rite.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三年，範鎮樂成，上其所製樂章三、鑄律十二、編鍾十二、鎛鍾一、衡一、尺一、斛一，響石為編磬十二、特磬一，簫、笛、塤、篪、巢笙、和笙各二，並書及圖法。

translations.literal: In the third year, Fan Zhen's music was completed; he submitted the three musical sections he had made, twelve cast pitch pipes, twelve arranged bells, one great bell, one steelyard, one measure, one hu, twelve arranged sonorous stones and one special sonorous stone from sounding stone, two each of pan-pipe, vertical flute, ocarina, chi, nest-sheng, and he-sheng, together with writings and diagrams of the methods.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 3 Fan Zhen finished his music and presented three hymn sections, twelve pitch pipes, twelve serial bells, one great bell, steelyard, ruler, and hu measure, twelve serial chimes plus one special chime, and two each of flute, vertical flute, ocarina, chi, nest-sheng, and he-sheng, with treatises and diagrams.

sentences.zh: 帝與太皇太后禦延和殿，詔執政、侍從、台閣、講讀官皆往觀焉。

translations.literal: The emperor and Grand Empress Dowager proceeded to the Yanhe Hall and ordered chief ministers, attendants, palace officials, and lecturing officials all to go observe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Grand Empress Dowager watched from Yanhe Hall and summoned ministers, attendants, palace officers, and lecturers to hear.

sentences.zh: 賜鎮詔曰：“朕惟春秋之後，禮樂先亡；

translations.literal: The edict granted to Zhen said: 'We consider that after the Spring and Autumn period, ritual and music were first lost.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Fan Zhen began: 'We reflect that after the Spring and Autumn era ritual and music were the first to perish.'

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，《韶》、《武》僅在。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward, Shao and Wu survived only in name.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han only the names of Shao and Wu remained.

sentences.zh: 散樂工於河、海之上，往而不還；

translations.literal: Dispersing music workers to the rivers and seas—they went and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians were scattered to the rivers and seas and never returned.

sentences.zh: 聘先生於齊、魯之間，有莫能致。

translations.literal: Inviting masters from Qi and Lu—none could be brought.
translations.idiomatic: Masters were invited from Qi and Lu, yet none could be obtained.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以下，曹、鄶無譏。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, Cao and Zheng went unblamed.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward the music of Cao and Zheng passed without reproach.

sentences.zh: 豈徒鄭、衛之音，已雜華、戎之器。

translations.literal: Was it only Zheng and Wei sounds that had already mixed with Hua and Rong instruments?
translations.idiomatic: It was not only Zheng and Wei melodies that had mingled with foreign instruments.

sentences.zh: 間有作者，猶存典刑。

translations.literal: Occasionally there were authors who still preserved canonical forms.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally a reformer still preserved canonical form.

sentences.zh: 然銖、黍之一差，或宮、商之易位。

translations.literal: Yet a difference of one millet grain in the pitch standard, or an easy shift between palace and shang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a millet-grain error in pitch, or an easy slip between palace and shang, could undo all.

sentences.zh: 惟我四朝之老，獨知五降之非。

translations.literal: Only our dynasty's elder of four reigns alone knew the error of the five descents.
translations.idiomatic: Only you, elder statesman of four reigns, truly knew the error of the five descents.

sentences.zh: 審聲知音，以律生尺。

translations.literal: Examining sound and knowing tone, from pitch generating measure.
translations.idiomatic: You examined sound, mastered tone, and derived measure from pitch.

sentences.zh: 覽詩書之來上，閱簨虡之在廷。

translations.literal: Perusing the Odes and Documents submitted above, reviewing the frames and stands in the court.
translations.idiomatic: You brought the Odes and Documents before us and set frames and stands in the court.

sentences.zh: 君臣同觀，父老太息。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers together observed; fathers and elders sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers watched together while elders sighed with emotion.

sentences.zh: 方詔學士、大夫論其法，工師、有司考其聲。

translations.literal: We shall order scholars and grandees to discuss the method, and craftsmen and officials to examine the sound.
translations.idiomatic: We shall have scholars debate the method and craftsmen test the sound.

sentences.zh: 上追先帝移風易俗之心，下慰老臣愛君憂國之誌。

translations.literal: Above it pursues the former emperor's wish to shift customs and improve manners; below it comforts the old minister's will to love the ruler and worry for the state.
translations.idiomatic: This fulfills the late emperor's wish to reform customs above and comforts your loyal concern for the realm below.

sentences.zh: 究觀所作，嘉歎不忘。”

translations.literal: Examining and observing what was made, he praised and sighed and did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: We have examined your work with admiration and hold it in lasting esteem.

sentences.zh: 鎮為《樂論》，其自敘曰：“臣昔為禮官，從諸儒難問樂之差謬，凡十餘事。

translations.literal: Zhen wrote Discourse on Music; in his own preface he said: 'Your servant formerly served as a ritual official and followed the various Confucians in questioning the errors and discrepancies in music—more than ten matters in all.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen wrote a Discourse on Music, explaining: 'When I served as a ritual official I joined other scholars in questioning errors in the music—more than ten points in all.'

sentences.zh: 厥初未習，不能不小牴牾。

translations.literal: At first, not yet practiced, I could not but have small contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: At first, being inexperienced, I could not avoid some inconsistencies.

sentences.zh: 後考《周官》、《王製》、司馬遷《書》、班氏《志》，得其法，流通貫穿，悉取舊書，去其牴牾。

translations.literal: Later I examined the Offices of Zhou, the Royal Regulations, Sima Qian's Records, and the Han Treatises, obtained their methods, made them flow and penetrate through, took all the old books, and removed their contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: Later I studied the Offices of Zhou, the Royal Regulations, Sima Qian's Records, and the Han treatises, mastered their methods, reconciled the texts, and removed their contradictions.

sentences.zh: 掇其要，作為八論。

translations.literal: Gathering the essentials, I made eight discourses.
translations.idiomatic: From their essentials I composed eight treatises.

sentences.zh: ”其《論律》、《論黍》、《論尺》、《論量》、《論聲器》，言在《律曆志》。

translations.literal: His Discourse on Pitch Pipes, Discourse on Millet Grain, Discourse on Measure, Discourse on Capacity, and Discourse on Sounding Vessels—their words are in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: His treatises on pitch pipes, millet grain, measure, capacity, and sounding vessels appear in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 《論鍾》曰：

translations.literal: The Discourse on Bells states:
translations.idiomatic: The Discourse on Bells reads:

sentences.zh: 夫鍾之製，《周官·鳧氏》言之甚詳，而訓解者其誤有三：若云：“帶，所以介，其名也介，在於、鼓、鉦、舞、甬、衡之間。

translations.literal: As for the manufacture of bells, the Bell Maker in the Offices of Zhou speaks of it in great detail, yet those who annotate it have three errors: as one says, 'The girdle is what separates; its name is separate; it lies between the yu, drum, zheng, dance, stem, and crossbeam.'
translations.idiomatic: Bell-making is described in detail in the Offices of Zhou, yet commentators err in three ways. One says the girdle 'separates' and lies between the yu, drum, zheng, dance, stem, and crossbeam.

sentences.zh: ”介於、鼓、鉦、舞之間則然，非在甬、衡之上，其誤一也。

translations.literal: That it lies between the yu, drum, zheng, and dance is so, but not above the stem and crossbeam—that is the first error.
translations.idiomatic: It is true between the yu, drum, zheng, and dance, but not above stem and crossbeam—that is the first error.

sentences.zh: 又云：“舞，上下促，以橫為修，從為廣，舞廣四分。

translations.literal: Again it says: 'The dance: upper and lower are shortened; taking the horizontal as the length, following as the width—the dance width is four parts.'
translations.idiomatic: A second comment says the dance section is shortened top and bottom, with horizontal length and vertical width each four parts.

sentences.zh: ”今亦去徑之二分以為之間，則舞間之方常居銑之四也。

translations.literal: Now if one also takes two parts of the diameter for the interval, then the square of the dance interval constantly occupies four parts of the bell mouth.
translations.idiomatic: If two parts of the diameter are taken for the interval, the dance interval's square always occupies four parts of the bell mouth.

sentences.zh: 舞間方四，則鼓間六亦其方也。

translations.literal: If the dance interval is square four, then the drum interval six is also its square.
translations.idiomatic: With the dance interval a square of four, the drum interval of six is likewise squared.

sentences.zh: 鼓六、鉦六、舞四，即言鼓間與舞佾相應，則鼓與舞皆六，所雲“鉦六、舞四”，其誤二也。

translations.literal: Drum six, zheng six, dance four—if it says the drum interval corresponds to the dance rows, then drum and dance are both six; what is said as 'zheng six, dance four' is the second error.
translations.idiomatic: Drum six, zheng six, dance four: if drum interval matches dance rows, drum and dance should both be six. To say 'zheng six, dance four' is the second error.

sentences.zh: 又云：“鼓外二，鉦外一。

translations.literal: Again it says: 'Outside the drum two, outside the zheng one.'
translations.idiomatic: A third comment says 'two outside the drum, one outside the zheng.'

sentences.zh: ”彼既以鉦、鼓皆六，無厚薄之差，故從而穿鑿，以遷就其說，其誤三也。

translations.literal: Since they already took zheng and drum as both six with no difference in thick and thin, they therefore forced the explanation to fit their doctrine—that is the third error.
translations.idiomatic: Having fixed zheng and drum at six with no thickness difference, they forced the text to fit their theory—the third error.

sentences.zh: 今臣所鑄編鍾十二，皆從其律之長，故鍾口十者，其長十六以為鍾之身。

translations.literal: Now the twelve arranged bells your servant casts all follow the length of their pitch pipes; thus for a bell mouth of ten, its length is sixteen for the bell body.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve serial bells I cast follow each pipe's length: a mouth of ten parts yields a body sixteen parts long.

sentences.zh: 鉦者，正也，居鍾之中，上下皆八，下去二以為之鼓，上去二以為之舞，則鉦居四而鼓與舞皆六。

translations.literal: The zheng is 'correct' and occupies the center of the bell; above and below are eight each; below, remove two to make the drum; above, remove two to make the dance—thus the zheng occupies four while drum and dance are each six.
translations.idiomatic: The zheng, meaning 'correct,' sits at the bell's center with eight parts above and below; two are removed below for the drum and two above for the dance, so zheng is four and drum and dance are six each.

sentences.zh: 是故於、鼓、鉦、舞、篆、景、欒、隧、甬、衡、旋蟲，鍾之文也，著於外者也；

translations.literal: Therefore the yu, drum, zheng, dance, seal, image, luan, tunnel, stem, crossbeam, and rotating worm are the bell's patterns, displayed on the outside.
translations.idiomatic: The yu, drum, zheng, dance, seal, image, luan, tunnel, stem, crossbeam, and worm pattern are the bell's outward ornament.

sentences.zh: 廣、長、空徑、厚、薄、大、小，鍾之數也，起於內者也。

translations.literal: Width, length, hollow diameter, thickness, thinness, large, and small are the bell's numbers, arising from within.
translations.idiomatic: Width, length, hollow diameter, thickness, and size are the bell's inner measurements.

sentences.zh: 若夫金錫之齊與鑄金之狀率按諸《經》，差之毫厘則聲有高下，不可不審。

translations.literal: As for the proportions of gold and tin and the condition of casting metal, all follow the classics; a difference of a hair's breadth and the sound has high and low—this must be examined carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-tin alloy and casting must follow the classics exactly; a hair's breadth changes pitch and cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 其鎛鍾亦以此法而四倍之。

translations.literal: The great bells also use this method quadrupled.
translations.idiomatic: Great bells follow the same method at four times the scale.

sentences.zh: 今太常鍾無大小、無厚薄、無金齊，一以黃鍾為率，而磨以取律之合，故黃鍾最薄而輕。

translations.literal: Now the Court's bells have no large or small, no thick or thin, no metal proportions; all take Yellow Bell as the standard and file to obtain agreement with the pitch pipes—therefore Yellow Bell is thinnest and lightest.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Court bells have no regulated size, thickness, or alloy but are all filed to Yellow Bell, making Yellow Bell thinnest and lightest.

sentences.zh: 自大呂以降，迭加重厚，是以卑陵尊，以小加大，其可乎？

translations.literal: From Great Lu downward they progressively add weight and thickness; thus the low overtops the high and the small is added to the large—can this be right?
translations.idiomatic: From Great Lu down they grow heavier and thicker, so lower tones overwhelm higher and smaller bells outweigh larger—can that be right?

sentences.zh: 且清聲者不見於《經》，惟《小胥》注云：“鍾磬者，編次之，二八十六枚而在一虡謂之堵。

translations.literal: Moreover clear tones are not seen in the classics; only the Small Steward commentary says: 'Bells and chime-stones are arranged in sequence; two times eight sixteen pieces in one frame is called a wall.'
translations.idiomatic: Clear subsidiary tones are not in the classics; only the Small Steward commentary says bells and chimes are arranged sixteen to a frame called a 'wall.'

sentences.zh: ”至唐又有十二清聲，其聲愈高，尤為非是。

translations.literal: By Tang there were again twelve clear tones; their sound was ever higher—especially wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang added twelve clear tones pitched even higher—especially wrong.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊有四清聲，置而弗用，至劉幾用之，與鄭、衛無異。

translations.literal: Our dynasty formerly had four clear tones, set aside and not used; when Liu Ji used them, they were no different from Zheng and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty once had four clear tones that were set aside; when Liu Ji revived them they resembled Zheng and Wei music.

sentences.zh: 《論磬》曰：

translations.literal: The Discourse on Chime-Stones states:
translations.idiomatic: The Discourse on Chime-Stones reads:

sentences.zh: 臣所造編磬，皆以《周官·磬氏》為法，若黃鍾股之博四寸五分，股九寸，鼓一尺三寸五分；

translations.literal: The arranged chime-stones your servant made all follow the Chime-Stone Maker in the Offices of Zhou as law; for example Yellow Bell: thigh width four inches five parts, thigh nine inches, drum one foot three inches five parts.
translations.idiomatic: My arranged chimes follow the Offices of Zhou Chime-Stone Maker: Yellow Bell's thigh is four inches five parts wide, nine inches long, with a drum one foot three inches five parts.

sentences.zh: 鼓之博三寸，而其厚一寸，其弦一尺三寸五分。

translations.literal: The drum's width three inches, its thickness one inch, its string one foot three inches five parts.
translations.idiomatic: The drum is three inches wide, one inch thick, with a string of one foot three inches five parts.

sentences.zh: 十二磬各以其律之長而三分損益之，如此其率也。

translations.literal: The twelve chime-stones each take the length of their pitch pipe and apply the rule of third increase and decrease—such is the proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve stones is sized by its pitch pipe through the rule of thirds increase and decrease.

sentences.zh: 今之十二磬，長短、厚薄皆不以律，而欲求其聲，不亦遠乎？

translations.literal: Today's twelve chime-stones: long, short, thick, and thin all do not follow the pitch pipes, yet one seeks their sound—is this not far off?
translations.idiomatic: Today's twelve stones vary in length and thickness without following the pipes, yet we expect correct pitch—how far is that from the mark?

sentences.zh: 鍾有齊也，磬，石也，天成之物也。

translations.literal: Bells have alloy proportions; chime-stones are stone, a thing completed by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Bells require regulated alloy; chimes are stone, a product of nature.

sentences.zh: 以其律為之長短、厚薄，而其聲和，此出於自然，而聖人者能知之，取以為法，後世其可不考正乎？

translations.literal: Making their long, short, thick, and thin according to their pitch pipes and their sound harmonious—this comes from nature, and the sage could know it, take it as law; should later ages not examine and correct it?
translations.idiomatic: Sizing them by pitch until they sound in harmony is natural; the sages knew this and made it law. Should later ages not verify it?

sentences.zh: 考正而非是，則不足為法矣。

translations.literal: If examination and correction are not correct, then it is insufficient to serve as law.
translations.idiomatic: If verification fails, the method is no true standard.

sentences.zh: 特磬則四倍其法而為之。

translations.literal: The special chime-stone then quadruples this method to make it.
translations.idiomatic: The special chime is made at four times this scale.

sentences.zh: 國朝祀天地、宗廟及大朝會，宮架內止設鎛鍾，惟後廟乃用特磬，非也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and great court assemblies, within the palace orchestra only sets great bells; only the rear temple used the special chime-stone—wrong.
