translations.idiomatic: In sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, the ancestors, and great court assemblies, the palace orchestra sets only great bells; only the rear temple used a special chime—incorrect.

sentences.zh: 今已升祔後廟，特磬遂為無用之樂。

translations.literal: Now that the rear temple has been elevated to joint enshrinement, the special chime-stone has become useless music.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the rear temple has been elevated, the special chime has become obsolete.

sentences.zh: 臣欲乞凡宮架內於鎛鍾後各加特磬，貴乎金石之聲小大相應。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to request that within every palace orchestra, after the great bells, a special chime-stone be added at each, so that metal and stone sounds large and small correspond.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each palace orchestra add a special chime after its great bells so metal and stone tones of different scales answer one another.

sentences.zh: 《論八音》曰：

translations.literal: The Discourse on the Eight Tones states:
translations.idiomatic: The Discourse on the Eight Tones reads:

sentences.zh: 匏、土、革、木、金、石、絲、竹，是八物者，在天地間，其體性不同而至相戾之物也。

translations.literal: Gourd, earth, hide, wood, metal, stone, silk, and bamboo—these eight materials in the space between Heaven and Earth have different physical natures and are things that reach mutual opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Gourd, earth, hide, wood, metal, stone, silk, and bamboo are eight materials between Heaven and Earth whose natures differ and even oppose one another.

sentences.zh: 聖人製為八器，命之商則商，命之宮則宮，無一物不同者。

translations.literal: The sage made eight instruments; commanded as Shang then Shang, commanded as palace then palace—no one thing was not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The sage fashioned eight instruments so that when commanded as Shang they sounded Shang and when as palace they sounded palace—none failed to match.

sentences.zh: 能使天地之間至相戾之物無不同，此樂所以為和而八音所以為樂也。

translations.literal: Able to make things that reach mutual opposition in the space between Heaven and Earth all not different—this is why music is harmony and the eight tones are music.
translations.idiomatic: To reconcile such opposing materials into one harmony is why music is called harmonious and the eight tones constitute true music.

sentences.zh: 樂下太常，而楊傑上言：“元豐中，詔範鎮、劉幾與臣詳議郊廟大樂，既成而奏，稱其和協。

translations.literal: The music was sent down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Yang Jie submitted a memorial saying: 'In Yuanfeng, an edict ordered Fan Zhen, Liu Ji, and your servant to deliberate in detail on suburban and temple great music; when completed and presented, it was called harmonious.'
translations.idiomatic: When the music reached the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Yang Jie memorialized: 'During Yuanfeng Fan Zhen, Liu Ji, and I deliberated suburban and temple music; when it was presented it was judged harmonious.'

sentences.zh: 今鎮新定樂法，頗與樂局所議不同。

translations.literal: Now Zhen's newly fixed music methods differ considerably from what the Music Bureau deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen's new methods differ greatly from what the Music Bureau had settled.

sentences.zh: 且樂經仁宗命作，神考睿斷，奏之郊廟、朝廷，蓋已久矣，豈可用鎮一說而遽改之？

translations.literal: Moreover the music classic was ordered made by Emperor Renzong and decided by the divine Emperor Shenzong; presented at suburban altars, temples, and court—already long; how can one use Zhen's single doctrine and abruptly change it?
translations.idiomatic: That music was commissioned by Emperor Renzong and ratified by Emperor Shenzong; it has long been performed at altars and court. How can Fan Zhen's single theory overturn it overnight?

sentences.zh: ”遂著《元祐樂議》以破鎮說。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the Yuanyou Music Discourse to refute Zhen's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote the Yuanyou Music Discourse to refute Fan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 其《議樂章》曰：

translations.literal: Its Discourse on Music Sections states:
translations.idiomatic: Its section on hymn titles reads:

sentences.zh: 國朝大樂所立曲名，各有成憲，不相淆雜，所以重正名也。

translations.literal: The tune names established for our dynasty's great music each have fixed statutes and do not mix confusedly—this is to honor correct naming.
translations.idiomatic: Our great music's tune names each follow fixed statutes without confusion, honoring correct naming.

sentences.zh: 故廟室之樂皆以“大”名之，如《大善》、《大仁》、《大英》之類是也。

translations.literal: Therefore temple music all takes 'Great' to name them, as in Great Goodness, Great Benevolence, Great Excellence, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Temple hymns therefore take Great in their titles, as in 'Great Goodness,' 'Great Benevolence,' and 'Great Excellence.'

sentences.zh: 今鎮以《文明之曲》獻祖廟，以《大成之曲》進皇帝，以《萬歲之曲》進太皇太后，其名未正，難以施於宗廟、朝廷。

translations.literal: Now Zhen with 'Tune of Civilized Brilliance' presents to the ancestral temple, with 'Tune of Great Completion' advances to the emperor, with 'Tune of Ten Thousand Years' advances to the Grand Empress Dowager—their names are not correct and are hard to apply at temples and court.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen offers 'Tune of Civilized Brilliance' to the ancestral temple, 'Tune of Great Completion' to the emperor, and 'Tune of Ten Thousand Years' to the Grand Empress Dowager—titles improper for temple and court.

sentences.zh: 《議宮架加磬》曰：

translations.literal: The Discourse on Adding Chime-Stones to the Palace Orchestra states:
translations.idiomatic: The section on adding chimes to the palace orchestra reads:

sentences.zh: 鎮言：“國朝祀天地、宗廟及大朝會，宮架內止設鎛鍾，惟後廟乃用特磬，非也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: 'Our dynasty in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, and great court assemblies, within the palace orchestra only sets great bells; only the rear temple used the special chime-stone—wrong.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen said: 'In sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, the ancestors, and great assemblies the orchestra sets only great bells; only the rear temple used a special chime—wrong.'

sentences.zh: 今已升後廟，特磬遂為無用之樂，欲乞凡宮架內於鎛鍾後各加特磬，貴乎金石之聲小大相應。

translations.literal: Now that the rear temple has been elevated, the special chime-stone has become useless music; it is wished to request that within every palace orchestra, after the great bells, a special chime-stone be added at each, so that metal and stone sounds large and small correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the rear temple is elevated, the special chime is obsolete; he asks to add a special chime after each orchestra's great bells so metal and stone answer in scale.

sentences.zh: ”按《唐六典》：天子宮架之樂，鎛鍾十二、編鍾十二、編磬十二，凡三十有六虡，宗廟與殿庭同。

translations.literal: According to the Tang Six Canon: the Son of Heaven's palace orchestra music had twelve great bells, twelve arranged bells, twelve arranged chime-stones—thirty-six frames in all; temples and palace halls were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Six Canon records the Son of Heaven's orchestra as twelve great bells, twelve serial bells, and twelve serial chimes—thirty-six frames—for temple and palace alike.

sentences.zh: 凡中宮之樂，則以大磬代鍾，餘如宮架之製。

translations.literal: For all inner-palace music, the great chime-stone replaced bells; the rest followed the palace orchestra system.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-palace music used a great chime in place of bells, with the rest as in the palace orchestra.

sentences.zh: 今以鎛鍾、特磬並設之，則為四十八架，於古無法。

translations.literal: Now if great bells and special chime-stones are both set up, it becomes forty-eight frames—with no method in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Setting both great bells and special chimes together would make forty-eight frames, for which antiquity offers no precedent.

sentences.zh: 皇帝將出，宮架撞黃鍾之鍾，右五鍾皆應；

translations.literal: When the emperor is about to go out, the palace orchestra strikes the Yellow Bell bell and the five bells on the right all respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor is about to depart, the orchestra strikes Yellow Bell and the five bells to the right answer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝興，宮架撞蕤賓之鍾，左五鍾皆應。

translations.literal: When the emperor rises, the palace orchestra strikes the Flanking Guest bell and the five bells on the left all respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rises, it strikes Flanking Guest and the five bells to the left answer.

sentences.zh: 未聞皇帝出入，以特磬為節。

translations.literal: I have not heard of the emperor entering and exiting with the special chime-stone as the beat.
translations.idiomatic: Nowhere is the emperor's entry and exit marked by a special chime.

sentences.zh: 《議十六鍾磬》曰：

translations.literal: The Discourse on the Sixteen Bells and Chime-Stones states:
translations.idiomatic: The section on sixteen bells and chimes reads:

sentences.zh: 鎮謂：“清聲不見於《經》，惟《小胥》注雲‘鍾磬者，編次之，十六枚而在一虡謂之堵。

translations.literal: Zhen said: 'Clear tones are not seen in the classics; only the Small Steward commentary says, "Bells and chime-stones are arranged in sequence; sixteen pieces in one frame is called a wall."'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen said clear tones are not in the classics and cited only the Small Steward note on sixteen bells or chimes per frame.

sentences.zh: ’至唐又有十二清聲，其聲愈高，尤為非是。

translations.literal: By Tang there were again twelve clear tones; their sound was ever higher—especially wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Tang's twelve clear tones were even higher and especially wrong.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊有四清聲，置而弗用，至劉幾用之，與鄭、衛無異。

translations.literal: Our dynasty formerly had four clear tones, set aside and not used; when Liu Ji used them, they were no different from Zheng and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated that our four clear tones, unused until Liu Ji revived them, resembled Zheng and Wei.

sentences.zh: ” 按編鍾、編磬十六，其來遠矣，豈徒見於《周禮·小胥》之注哉？

translations.literal: Examining arranged bells and chime-stones at sixteen—their origin is far distant; how are they seen only in the commentary to the Small Steward in the Rites of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: Yet sixteen bells or chimes are ancient; they are not found only in the Small Steward commentary.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝時，犍為郡於水濱得古磬十六枚，帝因是陳禮樂、《雅》《頌》之聲，以風化天下。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han, Qianwei commandery obtained sixteen ancient chime-stones by the water's edge; the emperor therefore displayed ritual music and the sounds of the Odes and Hymns to transform the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng of Han, Qianwei recovered sixteen ancient chimes from a riverbank, and the emperor used them to display ritual music and the Odes to transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 其事載於《禮樂志》，不為不詳，豈因劉幾然後用哉？

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Ritual and Music in detail—is it because of Liu Ji that they were then used?
translations.idiomatic: This is recorded fully in the Treatise on Ritual and Music. Did Liu Ji invent their use?

sentences.zh: 且漢承秦，秦未嚐製作禮樂，其稱古磬十六者，乃二帝、三王之遺法也。

translations.literal: Moreover Han succeeded Qin, and Qin never made ritual music; what is called the sixteen ancient chime-stones are the legacy methods of the Two Emperors and Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Han succeeded Qin, which never made ritual music; those sixteen stones were the legacy of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 其王樸樂內編鍾、編磬，以其聲律太高，歌者難逐，故四清聲置而弗用。

translations.literal: In Wang Pu's music the arranged bells and chime-stones, because their pitch was too high and singers could not pursue them, therefore the four clear tones were set aside and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu's serial bells and chimes were too high for singers, so the four clear tones were set aside.

sentences.zh: 及神宗朝下三律，則四清聲皆用而諧協矣。

translations.literal: When the divine Emperor Shenzong lowered three pitches, then the four clear tones were all used and harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong lowered the scale by three pitches, the four clear tones worked in harmony.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》曰：“鳧氏為鍾，薄厚之所震動，清濁之所由出。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: 'The Bell Maker makes bells; the vibration of thick and thin is where clear and muddy come forth.'
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says: 'The Bell Maker makes bells; from thick and thin vibration come clear and muddy tones.'

sentences.zh: ”則清聲豈不見於《經》哉？

translations.literal: Then are clear tones not seen in the classics?
translations.idiomatic: Are clear tones not in the classics after all?

sentences.zh: 今鎮以簫、笛、塤、篪、巢笙、和笙獻於朝廷，簫必十六管，是四清聲在其間矣。

translations.literal: Now Zhen with pan-pipe, vertical flute, ocarina, chi, nest-sheng, and he-sheng presents to the court; the pan-pipe must have sixteen tubes—then the four clear tones are among them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fan Zhen presents flutes, ocarinas, chi, and mouth-organs to court, and his pan-pipe has sixteen tubes—so the four clear tones are already there.

sentences.zh: 自古無十二管之簫，豈《簫韶》九成之樂已有鄭、衛之聲乎？

translations.literal: From antiquity there has been no twelve-tube pan-pipe—could the ninefold music of Shaoyao already have had Zheng and Wei sounds?
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity knew no twelve-tube pan-pipe. Did the nine movements of Shaoyao already contain Zheng and Wei?

sentences.zh: 禮部、太常亦言“鎮樂法自係一家之學，難以參用”，而樂如舊制。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices also said 'Zhen's music methods are the learning of a single school and hard to use together,' and music followed the old system.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and the Court also held that Fan Zhen's methods were a private school of thought unfit for official use, and music remained on the old system.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，始命大樂正葉防撰朝會二舞儀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Great Director of Music Ye Fang was first ordered to compose the protocols for the two dances of court assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yuanyou 4, Great Director of Music Ye Fang was ordered to draft protocols for the two court assembly dances.

sentences.zh: 武舞曰《威加四海之舞》：

translations.literal: The military dance is called the Dance of Might Spreading over the Four Seas:
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance was titled 'Might Spreading over the Four Seas:'

sentences.zh: 第一變：舞人去南表三步，總幹而立，聽舉樂，三鼓，前行三步，及表而蹲；

translations.literal: First change: dancers go from the southern marker three paces, grasp the staffs and stand, listen for the music to begin, three drumbeats, advance three paces, reach the marker and crouch.
translations.idiomatic: First section: dancers leave the southern marker three paces, grasp their staffs, and stand; at three drumbeats they advance three paces to the marker and crouch.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆舞，進一步，正立；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all dance, advance one pace, stand upright.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all dance forward one pace and stand upright.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆持幹荷戈，相顧作猛賁速趫之狀；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all hold staffs and bear halberds, look at one another making the posture of fierce warriors rushing swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all hold staffs and halberds and face one another in the posture of fierce warriors charging swiftly.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆轉身向裏，以幹戈相擊刺，足不動；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all turn inward, strike and stab with staff and halberd, feet not moving.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all turn inward and strike and thrust with staff and halberd without moving the feet.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆回身向外，擊刺如前；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all turn outward, strike and stab as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all turn outward and strike and thrust as before.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆正立舉手，蹲；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all stand upright and raise hands, crouch.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all stand upright, raise the hands, and crouch.

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat each turns to face the other, holding staff and halberd in a seated posture.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，各相擊刺；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat each strikes and thrusts at the other.

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all rise, gather staff and halberd as the image of victorious seizure.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆正麵，作猛賁趫速之狀；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all turn inward and strike and thrust without moving the feet.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，各轉身向外擊刺如前；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, each turns outward and strikes and stabs as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat each turns outward and strikes and thrusts as before.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆正立，蹲；

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆舞，進一步正立；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all dance forward and turn to face one another; at the next they straighten staff and halberd to depict mounting the platform to lecture on warfare.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆擊刺於東南；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all strike and stab toward the southeast.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆按盾舉戈，東南向而望，以象漳、泉奉土；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all press shield and raise halberd, gazing southeast to depict Zhang and Quan presenting territory.

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all press shield and raise halberd, gazing south to depict Hang and Yue coming to court; at the next all dance forward one pace and stand upright.

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all press shield and raise halberd, gazing northwest to depict the destruction of Bing and Fen.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆擊刺於正西；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all strike and thrust due west.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆按盾舉戈，西向而望，以象肅清銀、夏；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all press shield and raise halberd, gaze west, to image pacifying Yin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all press shield and raise halberd, gazing west to depict the pacification of Yin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆舞，進一步正跪，右膝至地，左足微起；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all dance, advance one pace and kneel upright, right knee to the ground, left foot slightly raised.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all dance forward and kneel with the right knee to the ground and the left foot slightly raised.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆置幹戈於地，各拱其手，象其不用；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all place staff and halberd on the ground, each cup hands, imaging that they are not used.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all set staff and halberd on the ground and cup the hands to show they are no longer used.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆左右舞蹈，象以文止武之意；

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all dance left and right, imaging the meaning of stopping warfare through culture.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all dance left and right to depict civil rule ending martial force.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆就拜，收其幹戈，起而躬立；

translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all bow, gather staff and halberd, rise, and stand with bowed bodies.

sentences.zh: 再鼓，皆舞，退，鼓盡即止，以象兵還振旅。

translations.literal: Second drumbeat, all dance and withdraw; when the drums end they stop, to image the army returning and marshaling the troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the second drumbeat all dance and withdraw; when the drums cease they stop, depicting the army's return and muster.

sentences.zh: 文舞曰《化成天下之舞》：

translations.literal: The civil dance is called the Dance of Transforming and Completing the World:
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance was titled 'Transforming and Completing the World:'

sentences.zh: 凡二舞綴表器及引舞振作，並與大祭祀之舞同。

translations.literal: For both dances, the attached markers, instruments, and lead dancers' movements are all the same as the great sacrificial dances.
translations.idiomatic: For both dances the markers, instruments, and lead dancers' movements matched those of the great sacrificial dances.

sentences.zh: 協律郎陳沂按閱，以謂節奏詳備，自是朝會則用之。

translations.literal: Pitch-Matching Officer Chen Yi examined and reviewed them, holding that the rhythm was detailed and complete; from then on they were used at court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch-Matching Officer Chen Yi reviewed them, judged the rhythm complete, and thereafter they were used at court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 八年，太常博士孫諤言：“臣嚐奉社稷之祠，親睹陳設，初疑其闕略而不備，退而考元祐祀儀，乃與所親見者合焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor Sun E said: 'Your servant once attended the altars of the state and soil, personally observing the arrangements; at first I doubted they were abbreviated and incomplete, but on retiring I examined the Yuanyou sacrificial protocols and they matched what I had personally seen.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 8, Sacrifices Doctor Sun E reported: 'I once attended the altars of soil and grain and at first thought the arrangements incomplete, but the Yuanyou protocols match what I saw.'

sentences.zh: 其登歌之樂，雖有鍾、磬、簨虡、搏拊、敔之屬，獨陳太社壇上，而太稷闕焉。

translations.literal: Its ascending song music, though it has bells, chime-stones, bamboo frames, clappers, and wooden beaters and the like, is set out only on the Great Soil altar while the Great Grain lacks them.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending song had bells, chimes, frames, clappers, and beaters, but they stood only on the Great Soil altar while the Great Grain altar had none.

sentences.zh: 夫宮架不備，非所以重社稷也。

translations.literal: That the palace orchestra is not complete is not how to honor the state and soil.
translations.idiomatic: An incomplete palace orchestra does not properly honor soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 《周官》製祭祀之法，則有靈鼓以鼓之，有幬犮舞以舞之，有太簇、應鍾、《鹹池》以極其歌舞之節，此樂文之備也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou in making the law of sacrifice had the spirit drum to beat it, had the shield-and-oxtail dance to dance it, had Great Cou, Responding Bell, and the Xian Pool to exhaust the sections of song and dance—this is the completeness of musical pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou prescribed spirit drums, shield dances, and hymns such as Great Cou, Responding Bell, and the Xian Pool to complete the music of these sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 唐社稷用二十架，至於開元，亦循三代之遺法，於壇之北，宮架備陳，別異天神，中建靈鼓，歌鍾、歌虡各設二壇，下舞上歌，何其盛也！

translations.literal: Tang soil and grain used twenty frames; down to Kaiyuan it also followed the legacy methods of the Three Dynasties; north of the altar the palace orchestra was fully set out, distinct from the Heavenly Spirit, with a spirit drum set in the center, and song bells and song frames each set on two altars—dance below and song above—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Tang used twenty frames for soil and grain; Kaiyuan followed the Three Dynasties with a full palace orchestra north of the altar, a central spirit drum, and separate song altars for bells and frames—dance below, song above—in magnificent array.

sentences.zh: 臣稽考典禮，凡祭太社、太稷，宜仿《周官》及《開元禮》文，於壇之北備設宮架，鍾、匏、竹各列二壇，南架之內，更植靈鼓。

translations.literal: Your servant examining canonical rites: for all sacrifices to Great Soil and Great Grain, one should imitate the Offices of Zhou and Kaiyuan ritual texts, north of the altar fully setting out the palace orchestra, bells, gourd, and bamboo each arranged on two altars; within the southern frames, further plant a spirit drum.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that sacrifices to Great Soil and Great Grain follow the Offices of Zhou and Kaiyuan by setting a full palace orchestra north of the altar, with bells, gourd, and bamboo on two altars each and a spirit drum within the southern frames.

sentences.zh: ”於是集侍從、禮官議增稷壇樂，而添用宮架之說不行。

translations.literal: Thereupon attendants and ritual officials were assembled to deliberate on increasing the music of the grain altar, but the proposal to add the palace orchestra was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Officials met to discuss expanding the grain altar music, but the proposal to add the palace orchestra was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 元符元年十一月，詔登歌、鍾、磬並依元豐詔旨，復先帝樂製也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanfu, an edict ordered that ascending song, bells, and chime-stones all follow the Yuanfeng edict and restore the former emperor's music system.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yuanfu 1 an edict restored ascending song, bells, and chimes to the Yuanfeng system of the late Emperor Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，詔前信州司法參軍吳良輔按協音律，改造琴瑟，教習登歌，以太常少卿張商英薦其知樂故也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, an edict ordered the former Judicial Assistant of Xinzhou Wu Liangfu to harmonize pitch pipes and remake qin and se, teaching ascending song—because Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Shangying recommended him for knowing music.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanfu 2 the former Xinzhou judicial assistant Wu Liangfu was ordered to harmonize pitch and remake zithers and harps for ascending song, on the recommendation of Vice Minister Zhang Shangying.

sentences.zh: 初，良輔在元豐中上《樂書》五卷，其書分為四類，以謂：“天地兆分，氣數爰定。

translations.literal: Initially, Liangfu in Yuanfeng submitted five volumes of Book of Music; the book was divided into four categories, holding that: 'Heaven and Earth first divided, and qi-numbers were then fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng, Liangfu had submitted five volumes of his Book of Music in four parts, arguing that 'Heaven and Earth first divided and breath-numbers were fixed.'

sentences.zh: 律厥氣數，通之以聲。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes are the qi-numbers; through them sound is communicated.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch pipes embody those breath-numbers and communicate through sound.

sentences.zh: 於是撰《釋律》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed Explication of Pitch Pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he wrote Explication of Pitch Pipes.

sentences.zh: 律為經，聲為緯。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes are the warp, sound the woof.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch is warp and sound is woof.

sentences.zh: 律以聲為文，聲以律為質。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes take sound as pattern; sound takes pitch pipes as substance.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch takes sound as its pattern and sound takes pitch as its substance.

sentences.zh: 旋相為宮，七音運生。

translations.literal: Rotating to make palace, the seven tones operate and generate.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating keys generate palace, and the seven tones proceed from one another.

sentences.zh: 於是撰《釋聲》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed Explication of Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he wrote Explication of Sound.

sentences.zh: 聲生於日，律生於辰，故經之以六律，緯之以五聲。

translations.literal: Sound is born from the day, pitch pipes from the chronogram; therefore the six pitch pipes are warp and the five tones woof.
translations.idiomatic: Sound arises from the day and pitch from the chronogram; the six pipes are warp and the five tones woof.

sentences.zh: 聲律相協，和而無乖。

translations.literal: Sound and pitch pipes mutually coordinate, harmonious without contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Sound and pitch coordinate in harmony without contradiction.

sentences.zh: 播之八音，八音以生。

translations.literal: Spread to the eight tones, the eight tones thereby generate.
translations.idiomatic: Spread to the eight tones, from which the eight categories arise.

sentences.zh: 於是撰《釋音》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed Explication of Tones.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he wrote Explication of Tones.

sentences.zh: 四物兼采，八器以成。

translations.literal: The four materials are jointly gathered; eight instruments thereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: Four classes of material are gathered and eight instruments thereby completed.

sentences.zh: 度數施設，象隱於形。

translations.literal: Numbers and measures are deployed; images are hidden in form.
translations.idiomatic: Measures are applied and images hidden in form.

sentences.zh: 考器論義，道德以明。

translations.literal: Examining instruments and discussing principles, the Way and virtue are thereby clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Examining instruments clarifies the Way and virtue.

sentences.zh: 於是撰《釋器》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed Explication of Instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he wrote Explication of Instruments.

sentences.zh: ”類各有條，凡四十四篇，大抵考之經傳，精以講思，頗益於樂理，文多，故弗著焉。

translations.literal: Each category has its entries, forty-four sections in all; mostly examining classics and commentaries, refined through reflection—quite beneficial to music theory; the text is lengthy, and therefore is not set forth here.
translations.idiomatic: Each part had its sections, forty-four in all, drawn from the classics and refined by reflection—useful to music theory, but too lengthy to reproduce here.

sentences.zh: 漢津至是年九十餘矣，本剩員兵士，自雲居西蜀，師事唐仙人李良，授鼎樂之法。

translations.literal: Han Jin by this year was over ninety; originally a surplus quota soldier, he himself said he dwelt in western Shu, studied under the Tang immortal Li Liang, and received the method of the tripod music.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Hanjin was over ninety. A surplus soldier from western Shu, he claimed to have studied under the Tang immortal Li Liang and learned the method of tripod music.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，漢津與房庶以善樂被薦，既至，黍律已成，阮逸始非其說，漢津不得伸其所學。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, Han Jin and Fang Shu were recommended for skill in music; when they arrived, the millet-grain pitch pipes were already completed, and Ruan Yi at first rejected their doctrine—Han Jin could not express what he had learned.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Hanjin and Fang Shu were recommended for musical skill, but millet-grain pitch pipes were already fixed and Ruan Yi rejected their views, so Hanjin could not advance his learning.

sentences.zh: 後逸之樂不用，乃退與漢津議指尺，作書二篇，敘述指法。

translations.literal: Later when Yi's music was not used, he retired and with Han Jin deliberated on finger measures, composing two books narrating fingering methods.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's music was abandoned, he withdrew and with Hanjin worked out finger measurements, writing two books on fingering technique.

sentences.zh: 漢津嚐陳於太常，樂工憚改作，皆不主其說。

translations.literal: Han Jin once presented this to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; music workers feared remaking and none upheld his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjin once presented this to the Court, but musicians feared remaking instruments and none supported him.

sentences.zh: 或謂漢津舊嚐執役於範鎮，見其製作，略取之，蔡京神其說而托於李良。

translations.literal: Some said Han Jin formerly served under Fan Zhen, saw his manufacture, and took from it in brief; Cai Jing made his doctrine divine and attributed it to Li Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Hanjin had served Fan Zhen, borrowed from his work, and that Cai Jing sanctified the theory by attributing it to Li Liang.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，禮部員外郎陳暘上所撰《樂書》二百卷，命禮部尚書何執中看詳，以謂暘欲考定音律，以正中聲，願送講議司，令知音律者參驗行之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, Ministry of Rites Outer Office Director Chen Yang submitted the two hundred volumes of Book of Music he had composed; the emperor ordered Minister of Rites He Zhizhong to examine them, holding that Yang wished to examine and fix pitch pipes to correct the central sound, and wished to send them to the Deliberation Office, ordering those who know pitch pipes to join in examining and implementing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yuanfu 2, Chen Yang of the Ministry of Rites submitted his two-hundred-volume Book of Music. Minister He Zhizhong was ordered to review it and proposed sending it to the Deliberation Office for experts to test Yang's plan to fix the central pitch.

sentences.zh: 暘之論曰：“漢津論樂，用京房二變、四清。

translations.literal: Yang's discourse said: 'Han Jin's discourse on music uses Jing Fang's two changes and four clear tones.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yang wrote: 'Wei Hanjin's music theory uses Jing Fang's two altered tones and four clear tones.'

sentences.zh: 蓋五聲十二律，樂之正也；

translations.literal: For the five tones and twelve pitch pipes are music's correctness.
translations.idiomatic: The five tones and twelve pitch pipes are the true music.

sentences.zh: 二變、四清，樂之蠹也。

translations.literal: The two changes and four clear tones are music's bane.
translations.idiomatic: The two altered tones and four clear tones are its corruption.

sentences.zh: 二變以變宮為君，四清以黃鍾清為君。

translations.literal: The two changes take altered palace as ruler; the four clear take clear Yellow Bell as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The altered tones make altered palace the ruler; the clear tones make clear Yellow Bell the ruler.

sentences.zh: 事以時作，固可變也，而君不可變；

translations.literal: Affairs may change with the times and thus can be altered, but the ruler cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs may change with the times, but the ruler cannot.

sentences.zh: 太簇、大呂、夾鍾，或可分也，而黃鍾不可分。

translations.literal: Great Cou, Great Lu, and Flanking Guest may perhaps be divided, but Yellow Bell cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Great Cou, Great Lu, and Flanking Guest might be subdivided, but Yellow Bell cannot.

sentences.zh: 豈古人所謂尊無二上之旨哉？

translations.literal: Is this not the ancients' meaning that in honor there are not two superiors?
translations.idiomatic: Does this not violate the ancient principle that honor admits no second sovereign?

sentences.zh: ”壬辰，詔曰：“朕惟隆禮作樂，實治內修外之先務，損益述作，其敢後乎？

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict said: 'We consider that exalting ritual and making music is truly the foremost task of governing within and cultivating without; how dare we be last in increase, decrease, narration, and creation?'
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day an edict declared: 'Exalting ritual and making music is the first task of inner governance and outer cultivation. How dare We delay reform?'

sentences.zh: 其令講議司官詳求曆代禮樂沿革，酌古今之宜，修為典訓，以貽永世，致安上治民之至德，著移風易俗之美化，乃稱朕谘諏之意焉。”

translations.literal: Let the officials of the Deliberation Office in detail seek the changes in ritual and music through the dynasties, weigh what is fitting in ancient and modern, revise canonical instructions to bequeath to eternal generations, achieve the utmost virtue of securing the realm and governing the people, display the beautiful transformation of shifting customs and improving manners—thus matching Our intent in consultation.'
translations.idiomatic: Let the Deliberation Office trace ritual and music through the dynasties, weigh ancient and modern practice, and compile canonical standards for all time—securing the realm, governing the people, and shifting customs as We intend.'

sentences.zh: 三年正月，漢津言曰：“臣聞黃帝以三寸之器名為《鹹池》，其樂曰《大卷》，三三而九，乃為黃鍾之律。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Han Jin stated: 'Your servant has heard that the Yellow Emperor with a three-inch instrument named it the Xian Pool; its music was called the Great Roll; three threes make nine—thus is the pitch pipe of Yellow Bell fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanfu 3, Hanjin reported: 'I have heard that the Yellow Emperor named a three-inch vessel the Xian Pool and its music the Great Roll; three times three is nine, and that fixes Yellow Bell.'

sentences.zh: 禹效黃帝之法，以聲為律，以身為度，用左手中指三節三寸，謂之君指，裁為宮聲之管；

translations.literal: Yu imitated the Yellow Emperor's method, taking sound as pitch pipes and the body as measure; using the left hand middle finger's three joints three inches, called the ruler finger, he cut the pipe for palace tone.
translations.idiomatic: Yu followed the Yellow Emperor, taking sound as pitch and the body as measure: the left middle finger's three joints of three inches, called the ruler finger, cut the palace pipe.

sentences.zh: 又用第四指三節三寸，謂之臣指，裁為商聲之管；

translations.literal: Again using the fourth finger's three joints three inches, called the minister finger, he cut the pipe for shang tone.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth finger's three joints of three inches, the minister finger, cut the shang pipe.

sentences.zh: 又用第五指三節三寸，謂之物指，裁為羽聲之管。

translations.literal: Again using the fifth finger's three joints three inches, called the things finger, he cut the pipe for yu tone.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth finger's three joints of three inches, the things finger, cut the yu pipe.

sentences.zh: 第二指為民、為角，大指為事、為徵，民與事，君臣治之，以物養之，故不用為裁管之法。

translations.literal: The second finger is people and jue; the great finger is affairs and zhi; people and affairs are governed by ruler and minister and nourished by things—therefore they are not used as methods for cutting pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The second finger stands for people and jue, the thumb for affairs and zhi; people and affairs are governed by ruler and minister and nourished by things, so they were not used to cut pipes.

sentences.zh: 得三指合之為九寸，即黃鍾之律定矣。

translations.literal: Obtaining the three fingers combined as nine inches, then the pitch pipe of Yellow Bell is fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The three fingers together make nine inches, and Yellow Bell is fixed.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾定，餘律從而生焉。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell fixed, the remaining pitch pipes are generated from it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yellow Bell is fixed, the remaining pitches follow.

sentences.zh: 臣今欲請帝中指、第四指、第五指各三節，先鑄九鼎，次鑄帝坐大鍾，次鑄四韻清聲鍾，次鑄二十四氣鍾，然後均弦裁管，為一代之樂製。”

translations.literal: Your servant now wishes to request the emperor's middle finger, fourth finger, and fifth finger each three joints, first cast the nine tripods, next cast the Imperial Seat great bell, next cast the four-rhyme clear-tone bells, next cast the twenty-four qi bells, and then equalize strings and cut pipes to make the music system of an age.
translations.idiomatic: I now ask to take three joints each from the emperor's middle, fourth, and fifth fingers, first cast the nine tripods, then the Imperial Seat great bell, then the four-rhyme clear bells, then the twenty-four seasonal bells, and thereafter tune strings and cut pipes for the music of the age.'

sentences.zh: 其後十三年，帝一日忽夢人言：“樂成而鳳凰不至乎！

translations.literal: Thirteen years later, one day the emperor suddenly dreamed a man saying: 'Music is complete yet the phoenix has not come!'
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later the emperor dreamed a voice saying: 'The music is finished, yet the phoenix has not come!'

sentences.zh: 蓋非帝指也。

translations.literal: It is probably not the emperor's finger.
translations.idiomatic: 'It was not the emperor's finger.'

sentences.zh: ”帝寤，大悔歎，謂：“崇寧初作樂，請吾指寸，而內侍黃經臣執謂‘帝指不可示外人’，但引吾手略比度之，曰：‘此是也。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke and greatly regretted and sighed, saying: 'In the beginning of Chongning when music was made, they requested my finger measure, but the inner attendant Huang Jingchen held that the emperor's finger cannot be shown to outsiders—he only drew my hand and roughly compared measures, saying, "This is it."'
translations.idiomatic: Awakening, he sighed with deep regret: 'When Chongning music was made they asked for my finger, but the eunuch Huang Jingchen said the emperor's finger must not be shown outsiders. He only drew my hand and said, "This will do."'

sentences.zh: ’蓋非人所知。

translations.literal: Probably not what people know.
translations.idiomatic: 'That was not what people know.'

sentences.zh: 今神告朕如此，且奈何？

translations.literal: Now the spirit tells Us thus—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: 'Now the spirit tells me this. What can be done?'

sentences.zh: ”於是再出中指寸付蔡京，密命劉昺試之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again produced the middle finger measure and gave it to Cai Jing, secretly ordering Liu Bing to test it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore produced his middle finger again, gave the measure to Cai Jing, and secretly ordered Liu Bing to test it.

sentences.zh: 時昺終匿漢津初說，但以其前議為度，作一長笛上之。

translations.literal: At that time Bing ultimately concealed Han Jin's initial doctrine, but took his earlier deliberation as the standard and made one long vertical flute and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Bing hid Hanjin's original teaching and, using the earlier standard, made a long flute and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝指寸既長於舊，而長笛殆不可易，以動人觀聽，於是遂止。

translations.literal: The emperor's finger measure being longer than the old, and the long flute could hardly be changed without moving people's sight and hearing, thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor's finger was longer than the old measure and changing the long flute would disturb public performance, the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 蓋京之子絛雲。

translations.literal: Probably Jing's son Tiao spread the word.
translations.idiomatic: This was probably spread by Cai Jing's son Tiao.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，景鍾成。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, the Image Bell was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Image Bell was completed.

sentences.zh: 景鍾者，黃鍾之所自出也。

translations.literal: The Image Bell is what Yellow Bell comes forth from.
translations.idiomatic: The Image Bell was the source from which Yellow Bell proceeded.

sentences.zh: 垂則為鍾，仰則為鼎。

translations.literal: Hanging down it is a bell; lifting up it is a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Hanging down it served as a bell; turned up it became a tripod.

sentences.zh: 鼎之大，終於九斛，中聲所極。

translations.literal: The tripod's size ends at nine hu—a limit of the central sound.
translations.idiomatic: The tripod's capacity reached nine hu, the limit of the central tone.

sentences.zh: 製煉玉屑，入於銅齊，精純之至，音韻清越。

translations.literal: Refined jade dust was mixed into the copper alloy; at utmost purity the tone was clear and piercing.
translations.idiomatic: Refined jade dust was mixed into the copper until the tone rang clear and bright.

sentences.zh: 其高九尺，拱以九龍，惟天子親郊乃用之。

translations.literal: Its height is nine feet, arched with nine dragons; only when the Son of Heaven personally performs the suburban sacrifice is it used.
translations.idiomatic: Nine feet high and arched with nine dragons, it was used only when the Son of Heaven performed the suburban sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 立於宮架之中，以為君圍。

translations.literal: Set in the center of the palace orchestra as the ruler's enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: It stood at the center of the palace orchestra as the sovereign's enclosure.

sentences.zh: 於是命翰林學士承旨張康國為之銘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts Zhang Kangguo was ordered to compose an inscription for it.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zhang Kangguo was ordered to inscribe it.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：“天造我宋，於穆不已。

translations.literal: Its text says: 'Heaven made our Song, grand and unceasing.'
translations.idiomatic: The inscription read: 'Heaven made our Song, grand and unceasing.'

sentences.zh: 四方來和，十有二紀。

translations.literal: The four directions come in harmony—ten and two chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: 'The four quarters come in harmony through twelve chronograms.'

sentences.zh: 樂象厥成，維其時矣。

translations.literal: Music images its completion—this is its time.
translations.idiomatic: 'Music images its completion—this is its season.'

sentences.zh: 迪惟有夏，度自禹起。

translations.literal: Following the age of Xia, measures began from Yu.
translations.idiomatic: 'Following Xia, measures began with Yu.'

sentences.zh: 我龍受之，天地一指。

translations.literal: Our dragon received it; Heaven and Earth are one finger.
translations.idiomatic: 'Our dragon received them; Heaven and Earth share one measure.'

sentences.zh: 於論景鍾，中聲所止。

translations.literal: In discussing the Image Bell, the central sound stops.
translations.idiomatic: 'In the Image Bell the central sound finds its rest.'

sentences.zh: 有作於斯，無襲於彼。

translations.literal: Made in this age, not inherited from that.
translations.idiomatic: 'Made in this age, not copied from another.'

sentences.zh: 九九以生，律呂根柢。

translations.literal: Nine nines to generate—the root and foundation of pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: 'Nine nines generate—the root of pitch pipes.'

sentences.zh: 維此景鍾，非弇非侈。

translations.literal: This Image Bell is neither muffled nor extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: 'This Image Bell is neither muffled nor extravagant.'

sentences.zh: 在宋之庭，屹然中峙。

translations.literal: In the Song court it stands towering in the center.
translations.idiomatic: 'In the Song court it towers at the center.'

sentences.zh: 天子萬年，既多受祉。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ten thousand years—receiving many blessings.
translations.idiomatic: 'May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years and receive many blessings.'

sentences.zh: 維此景鍾，上帝命爾。

translations.literal: This Image Bell—High God commands you.
translations.idiomatic: 'This Image Bell—High God commands you.'

sentences.zh: 其承伊何，以燕翼子。

translations.literal: What does it continue? To give peace to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: 'What does it continue? Peace for descendants.'

sentences.zh: 永言寶之，宋樂之始。”

translations.literal: Forever treasure it—the beginning of Song music.
translations.idiomatic: 'Treasure it forever—the beginning of Song music.'
